title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
desc: Scoring functions built with advanced deep learning algorithms have recently gained prominence in protein–ligand pose generation and binding affinity prediction for computational drug design. However, several shortcomings make it increasingly difficult to evaluate scoring functions for a specific task across studies. Transparent disclosure of training data, code and procedures is essential to permit reproducibility, reuse and independent scrutiny. Guarding against data leakage, sampling bias and flawed design is equally important. Meaningful comparisons of scoring functions also require common data splits, checks for run-to-run variability and performance baselines. Here we propose a set of guidelines to help the community identify the most promising methods for addressing these important problems. Ballester and Tran-Nguyen advocate for transparency in data, code and experimental procedures in the evaluation of protein–ligand predictions. They discuss good practices for preventing data leakage and bias, enabling fair, reproducible and meaningful comparisons across different scoring methods.

title: Redefining drug discovery: AI-driven strategies for efficient cancer therapeutics.
desc: [Frontiers in oncology] The practice of artificial intelligence has recently expanded several social spheres, with the pharmaceutical domain leading the way. Given that AI can facilitate rational drug design, it is plausible to envision its involvement in developing pharmaceutical products from the laboratory to the patient's bedside. AI recognizes hit and lead compounds, followed by validation of therapeutic targets and optimization of molecular design. Artificial intelligence significantly impacts drug discovery and development processes, including target identification, molecule design, drug-drug interactions, drug repurposing, optimization of clinical trials, drug toxicity prediction, drug formulation, and delivery. AI-assisted approaches are progressively being employed for identification and prioritization of targets, biomarker discovery and virtual screening as well as prediction for the interaction of protein and ligand and their molecular properties followed by ADMET screening, molecular design and repurposing to be suited for clinical trial optimization. The significance of automation will be boosted by adopting the most recent artificial intelligence-based technologies, reducing the time it takes for drugs to be available in the market with improved quality, production process safety, and resource utilization. The application of artificial intelligence may not only aid in rapid decision-making but can also enhance the process of incorporating the newly discovered drug into the optimum dosage form, which leads to faster manufacturing of higher-quality drugs and ensures consistency among batches. The potential of artificial intelligence in drug discovery and development, has been explored in this review, encircling several stages from identification of target to its clinical applications, followed by drug development approaches encompassing the future of artificial intelligence in the pharmaceutical sector, along with crosstalk on the tools and tactics used to enforce artificial intelligence, current difficulties, and respective solutions.

title: Generative AI-Assisted Teaching and Clinical Reasoning Among TCM Interns
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Taipei City Hospital; conditions: Clinical, Education; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 38; status: COMPLETED] This study evaluated the effects of generative artificial intelligence (GAI)-assisted education on clinical reasoning performance among traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) interns. An assessor-blinded, nonrandomized, cluster-controlled educational intervention study was conducted at three hospital branches in Taiwan. Participants were assigned to either a GAI-assisted education group or a conventional education group according to their clinical training sites. The intervention group received a three-hour introductory training session on ChatGPT and was encouraged to use the tool independently for clinical case analysis during subsequent clinical rotations. The control group received conventional clinical education without structured GAI-assisted training. The primary outcome was clinical reasoning performance, assessed through clinical case reports independently evaluated by two blinded TCM educators. Secondary outcomes included perceptions of the four-element TCM diagnostic framework and perceptions of GAI-assisted learning.

title: Visualizing and Interpreting Temporal Care Team Dynamics for Cancer Survival Risk Analysis
desc: Cancer care is a longitudinal, time-sensitive process requiring coordination among diverse healthcare professionals (HCPs), whose collaboration evolves throughout treatment. Prior studies link care team structure to patient outcomes, but the temporal dynamics of collaboration and their relationship to evolving patient risk remain poorly understood. We introduce a visual analytics framework for modeling and interpreting time-varying care team interactions in oncology. We construct dynamic collaboration networks from electronic health record (EHR)-mediated communication data and use a temporal graph neural network (TGNN) to estimate patient outcome risk over time. We then investigate how changes in care team composition and specialist participation relate to shifts in estimated risk across treatment stages. Our multi-view interactive system combines TGNN-based risk modeling with coordinated visualizations of care team networks, feature-level explanations from a surrogate logistic regression model, and exploratory what-if analysis. Without making causal claims, the system helps analysts examine how risk estimates co-evolve with collaboration patterns and identify care team characteristics associated with these changes. We demonstrate its utility through expert-guided analysis scenarios involving 505 patients with breast, colorectal, and lung cancers, evaluating its ability to reveal clinically meaningful collaboration patterns. This work improves the interpretability of temporal graph-based models in longitudinal, team-based healthcare, with potential applicability to other evolving collaborative settings.

title: Explainable Multimodal AI for In-Hospital Detection of Lung Cancer and Heart Failure Using Routine Data: Development, Internal Validation, and Simulated Federated Evaluation
desc: Objective: To determine whether combining four routine data sources improves in-hospital detection of lung cancer and heart failure, which sources drive each prediction, whether explanations are faithful, whether models are fair, and how much benefit federated training retains. Methods: In this retrospective single-centre study, we linked MIMIC-IV admissions (73,637 patients) to chest radiographs, radiology reports, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) and laboratory tests from the first 48 hours. For each disease, excluding prior cases, we compared single-source models, gradient boosting and early, late and attention-based fusion on patient-level splits. We tested explanations for faithfulness and weight dependence, audited performance by sex, age, race and ethnicity, and insurance, and simulated five unequal hospitals to compare federated, centralised and local training. Results: Lung cancer was coded in 1.7% and heart failure in 15.6% of patients. For lung cancer, attention fusion reached an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.833 (95% CI 0.809-0.859) against 0.753 for gradient boosting on laboratory data; for heart failure, 0.885 (0.878-0.892) against 0.794 (both p < 0.001). Early and late fusion performed similarly. Laboratory data and radiology reports contributed most to lung cancer, and the ECG to heart failure. Explanations passed a deletion test; a weight-randomisation check on absolute attributions passed for ECG but not for laboratory explanations. For heart failure, discrimination fell with age. Federated training recovered 95% of the centralised gain over local training for heart failure; for lung cancer, federated averaging (FedAvg) recovered 51% and FedProx 82%. Conclusion: Fusing routine data improved in-hospital detection of both diseases over laboratory data alone, and which data matter depends on the disease. Explanation checks should be run per source and per similarity measure, and performance in older patients monitored. For the rare outcome, FedProx, which limits drift between sites, retained more of the pooled benefit than FedAvg. External validation is needed.

title: EG-BINN: Parameter-Efficient Ensembling of Gated Biologically Informed Neural Networks for Epigenetic Age Estimation
desc: Epigenetic aging clocks are widely used to evaluate biological aging, disease risk, and clinical interventions. However, most existing clocks rely on linear models that overlook nonlinear relationships between age and methylation patterns, or on deep learning architectures that are parameter-intensive and difficult to interpret. We developed EG-BINN, a parameter-efficient ensemble of biologically informed neural networks that uses sample-specific gating to modulate representations across biologically annotated nodes. Trained on 93 multi-tissue datasets, EG-BINN achieved the lowest mean and median absolute errors among matched linear and nonlinear baselines in five-fold cross-validation, as well as the lowest mean absolute and root mean squared errors across eight held-out Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets. Analysis of the gating mechanism revealed widespread associations between pathway gate values and age, including trajectories that varied across blood, adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, and liver. Across 11 TCGA cohorts, EG-BINN identified significant tumor--normal differences in residual epigenetic age acceleration in six cohorts, whereas Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) highlighted recurrent pathway nodes contributing to tumor age predictions. EG-BINN combines accurate pan-tissue age prediction with an explainable architecture for examining biologically labeled nodes across age, tissue, and disease contexts.

title: Advances and applications of engineered protein therapeutics and their role in precision medicine.
source: PubMed · Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology
desc: [Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology] Proteins are a vital class of biomolecules. They play essential roles in biological processes, including building cellular structures, forming cellular channels and receptors, catalyzing biological reactions, transporting molecules, and contributing to immune defense mechanisms. Advances in protein engineering have enabled the genetic modification of naturally occurring proteins, using recombinant deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) technology, leading to the development of therapeutic proteins with enhanced specificity, stability, and clinical performance. Despite the rapid growth of engineered biologics, a comprehensive understanding of how these innovations intersect with precision medicine remains limited. This review addresses this gap by summarizing the major contemporary approaches used in therapeutic protein engineering, including directed evolution, rational design, and de novo protein design, and by analyzing their roles in enabling patient-tailored interventions. It provides an integrated overview of the clinical applications of engineered therapeutic proteins across key medical fields, supported by a list of U.S. Food and Drug Administration- and European Medicines Agency-approved protein therapeutics from 2020 to 2025. The review further provides a comparative perspective on major protein engineering strategies, highlighting their relative advantages and limitations, while examining differences in clinical translation across major disease areas. By combining technological advances with disease-specific applications, this review offers a perspective that has not been fully developed in the literature. Finally, the review discusses the current challenges affecting the implementation of precision medicine, including immunogenicity, regulatory constraints, and ethical considerations, and outlines future directions, such as artificial intelligence-guided protein design, targeted protein degradation, and personalized vaccine development. Collectively, these insights highlight the expanding role of engineered proteins in shaping the next-generation of precision therapeutics and emphasize the growing importance of integrating multidisciplinary approaches to advance therapeutic innovation in modern clinical practice.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Versus Conventional Guided Implant Planning in Free End Saddle Cases
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Mariam Morcos Nasr; conditions: Partial Edentulism Class 1 or Class 2; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 20; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This study aims to compare the accuracy and clinical performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted implant planning with conventional human-based implant planning in patients presenting with free-end saddle edentulous areas requiring dental implant rehabilitation. Preoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images and intraoral scans will be used to assess the available bone, anatomical landmarks, and prosthetically driven implant positions. Implant planning and surgical guide fabrication will be performed using standardized digital workflows under the supervision of an experienced implant planning specialist. Postoperative CBCT imaging will be used to evaluate deviations between the planned and actual implant positions. The study will assess the accuracy of both planning approaches to determine whether AI-assisted planning provides comparable or improved implant placement accuracy relative to conventional planning.

title: Overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1: Patient-Specific Phenotype Concept Recognition in Full-Text Biomedical Literature
desc: Automatic phenotype information extraction plays an important role in rare disease diagnosis, genotype-phenotype analysis, and precision medicine. However, accurately identifying phenotype concepts and determining their associations with specific patients remain challenging, particularly in full-text biomedical articles involving multiple patients and complex clinical descriptions. This paper presents an overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1, which aims to promote the development of methods for patient-specific phenotype concept recognition from full-text biomedical literature. The task consists of two subtasks: full-text phenotype concept recognition and patient-specific phenotype association. For this evaluation, we used 200 annotated full-text biomedical articles from the PatientPheX dataset, containing 506 patients, 15,193 phenotype mentions, and 5,656 patient-phenotype associations. A total of 455 teams registered for the competition, with 189 and 103 valid submissions received on the Phase A and Phase B leaderboards, respectively. The best-performing system achieved an overall score of 0.7389 on the final test set, outperforming the baseline by 8.37 percentage points. The top-performing teams explored diverse approaches combining biomedical language models, large language models (LLMs), and ensemble strategies. The evaluation results highlight both the potential of these approaches and the remaining challenges in patient attribution and phenotype normalization from full-text biomedical literature. The post-evaluation phase remains open at https://tianchi.aliyun.com/competition/entrance/532512.

title: Quantifying Reproducibility of Common Laboratory Tests in a Tertiary Care Hospital for More Realistic Synthetic Data in Machine Learning
desc: Data from medical records are often limited in size, creating challenges for Artificial Intelligence training, and an opportunity for data augmentation techniques to create synthetic data. A natural question is how much data can be randomized and still be realistic. The main goal of this study is to attempt to measure the reproducibility of labs drawn in practice, so these ranges can be used for generating more realistic synthetic data. A second goal is to inform clinicians of the real error ranges of their laboratory data so these values may be better interpreted.

title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Framework for Early- versus Late-Stage Classification of Breast Cancer from Gene Expression, with Co-expression Network Analysis
desc: Anatomical stage is a principal determinant of treatment and prognosis in breast cancer, yet it is unclear how much information about stage is carried by the transcriptome of the primary tumour. We asked whether an a priori panel of 65 cancer-related genes can distinguish early-stage (AJCC Stage I-II) from late-stage (Stage III-IV) breast cancer, and which genes contribute to any signal. RNA-seq expression and pathologic stage for The Cancer Genome Atlas breast invasive carcinoma cohort (TCGA-BRCA) were obtained from the UCSC Xena platform. After restricting the data to primary tumours with a known stage, 1,075 tumours were analysed (805 early, 270 late) and split into stratified training (n = 860) and held-out test (n = 215) sets. Logistic regression, a support vector machine, random forest and gradient boosting were tuned by stratified five-fold cross-validation, with median imputation, standardisation and SMOTE oversampling fitted on training data only and classification thresholds chosen on out-of-fold training predictions. On the test set, Logistic Regression had the highest ROC-AUC, 0.618 (95% CI 0.530-0.704), with balanced accuracy 0.578, sensitivity 0.741 and specificity 0.416; differences in AUC between models were not statistically significant (DeLong p = 0.199-0.585). Permutation importance in the Gradient Boosting model ranked POU5F1, FLT3 and NOTCH1 highest, but this model's AUC confidence interval included 0.5, so the ranking is exploratory. No gene was differentially expressed between stage groups after false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction (smallest FDR = 0.057, CD44). A co-expression network built from training tumours identified REL, EP300 and ESR1 as the most connected genes, a property that reflects co-expression rather than regulation or association with stage. Limitations include a single cohort, no external validation, no clinical covariates and a small number of late-stage test tumours. Expression of this gene panel carries limited but measurable information about anatomical stage; expression-based stage models should be combined with clinicopathological variables and validated in independent cohorts before any clinical application is considered.

title: Knowledge Graphs for Cervical Cancer Across the Care Continuum: From Vaccination and Screening to Personalized Therapy.
source: PubMed · Therapeutics and clinical risk management
desc: [Therapeutics and clinical risk management] Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related death among women worldwide, with a disproportionately high burden in low- and middle-income countries. Infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) is the central etiological factor. Although HPV vaccination and standardized screening can substantially reduce incidence and mortality, major bottlenecks persist in real-world settings, including inadequate coverage, loss to follow-up, data silos, and limited interpretability of algorithms. Knowledge graphs (KGs), characterized by their core "entity-relation" structure, can integrate electronic medical records, HPV genotyping, pathology/imaging, multi-omics, and public health data within a unified semantic framework, and provide traceable evidence chains and reasoning pathways to support clinical decision-making. KGs may become an important enabler. This review summarizes the potential mechanisms and application paradigms of KGs along the full continuum of cervical cancer prevention and care, including primary prevention (vaccination strategies and health education), screening and diagnosis (multimodal data integration, explainable AI, and clinical decision support systems, CDSS), as well as therapeutic decision-making and follow-up management (molecular subtyping, drug associations, and recurrence monitoring. We further highlight key challenges such as ontology standardization, cross-institutional interoperability, dynamic knowledge updating, and reliability of automated knowledge extraction. Future work should focus on establishing reusable, engineering-oriented pathways for the synergy of "KG + large language models (LLMs)/multimodal AI", the development of explainability evaluation metrics, privacy-compliant frameworks, and deployable solutions for primary care settings, in order to accelerate progress toward the global cervical cancer elimination goal.

The study will also explore nurses' views on the clinical acceptability and usability of the decision-support system through semi-structured interviews.

title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
desc: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) models are often shared without their training data, assuming this protects the patients who contributed them. However, a model can reveal whether a patient's records were used in training, a privacy breach known as a membership inference attack. This risk is usually reported as a cohort average, which can appear negligible while individual patients are almost certainly exposed. Identifying potentially vulnerable records before developing a production model could make privacy assessment more practical. We measured each patient's vulnerability to membership inference attack, across 7,789 models trained on six clinical datasets in four modalities, including two adapted pretrained medical models. Training choices changed how many patients had high attack scores, but the patients who ranked highest by risk largely stayed the same across the configurations we tested. Stronger weight decay reduced the exposed cohort up to threefold, yet largely the same patients remained most at risk across training recipes, architectures and initializations, including foundation models. Therefore, we developed a lightweight screening tool that uses four small models to identify patients with high risk of exposure before production-model training. We also assessed if flagged patients could be protected without removing their data. Privacy screening should become incorporated into data preparation for clinical AI.

title: Computational Profiling and Pathogenicity Assessment of VHL Missense Mutations
desc: Mutations in the VHL tumor suppressor gene promote tumorigenesis by stabilizing HIF-1. In this study, we investigated the functional impact of VHL missense mutations using AlphaMissense pathogenicity scores, protein stability simulations, and molecular dynamics. AlphaMissense identified high pathogenicity scores for residues 60-200, including the {beta}-domain and HIF-binding domain, suggesting these regions are critical for VHL's tumor suppressor function. We categorized the mutations into two groups: those that primarily destabilize protein folding and those that likely disrupt VHL-HIF-1 binding. FoldX stability simulations revealed high {Delta}{Delta}G values for both groups, with proline substitutions exerting significant structural stress. Structural modeling confirmed that these mutations disrupt secondary structures, particularly {beta}-sheets. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that the VHL monomer is flexible and unstable in several regions, whereas the VHL-HIF complex, particularly the HIF-binding domain, exhibits enhanced stability. Mutational scanning revealed that bulky amino acid substitutions, such as tryptophan, cause notable destabilization. Interestingly, some mutations predicted to be structurally stable were still classified as pathogenic by AlphaMissense and validated in the literature, suggesting that pathogenicity may arise from subtle functional impairments rather than just structural instability. These findings underscore the value of combining machine learning, structural simulations, and experimental data to predict and interpret the pathogenicity of VHL mutations.

title: Large Language Model Framework for Structured Biomarker Extraction and Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Identification From Pathology Reports: Development and Evaluation Study.
desc: [JMIR formative research] Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive molecular subtype of breast cancer that needs to be identified accurately from pathology reports to inform decision-making. Large language models (LLMs) have been reported to show great potential in the automatic extraction of important oncology information from unstructured medical text. We aimed to create and test an LLM-based approach for automatic biomarker extraction and TNBC subtype classification based on breast cancer pathology reports using prompt-engineering techniques. In total, 532 breast cancer pathology reports from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were used. Our approach extracted structured oncology features, such as estrogen receptor status, progesterone receptor status, HER2 status, tumor size, tumor grade, and tumor histology, which were used to identify TNBC. We tested 4 frontier models: GPT-4o mini (released July 18, 2024), GPT-4.1 nano (released April 14, 2025), GPT-5 nano (released August 7, 2025), and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite. The designed framework was able to extract relevant biomarkers and clinicopathological attributes from unstructured pathology reports and allowed for the automated identification of patients with TNBC. Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite showed superior performance in the extraction of clinicopathological attributes. For all models investigated, chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting was shown to outperform other strategies, such as zero-shot and few-shot prompting, for both biomarker extraction and TNBC classification. GPT-4o mini using CoT prompts reported the highest performance for TNBC classification. Using prompt-engineering techniques based on LLMs proved to be an efficient method of translating unstructured breast cancer pathology reports into structured clinical information. Moreover, it can be used to accurately identify the TNBC subtype.

title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
desc: Early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma is critical to preserve access to curative treatment options. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) provides a standardized framework for non-invasive diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, based on major visual imaging features. However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS (p = 0.04)...

title: UnibindMD: An Integrated AI and Molecular Dynamics Platform for De Novo Peptide Binder Design
desc: UnibindMD is an integrated computational platform that turns a protein target into validated de novo peptide-binder leads by chaining five orthogonal stages: deep-learning binder design (BindCraft), independent structure prediction and confidence assessment (AlphaFold3-class / Boltz-2), binding-affinity prediction (PRODIGY), developability profiling (ADMET-AI), and all-atom molecular-dynamics validation (GROMACS/CHARMM36m). The platform targets a persistent weakness of single-method design, namely that confidence metrics such as ipTM and pLDDT are self-consistent but not independent, so a design predicted to be confident may still be physically unstable. We demonstrate UnibindMD on three Andes virus (ANDV) intervention points, a setting of urgent need given a case fatality rate approaching 40%, a 2026 MV Hondius cruise-ship outbreak (13 cases, 3 deaths), and no approved therapeutic: the Gn-Gc glycoprotein complex (viral entry), the L-protein endonuclease domain (cap-snatching; PDB 6Q99), and the host VEGFR2 kinase (vascular permeability; PDB 2XIR). Across nine BindCraft campaigns (4,475 trajectories) the platform produced 464 accepted binders (acceptance 2.3-67.6%), with top candidates reaching ipTM = 0.94 and pLDDT = 0.94. The three selected leads were predicted by PRODIGY to bind with G = -9.1 to -11.1 kcal mol-1 (Kd 8 nM-0.2 M), and all three remained stably bound over 100 ns of unrestrained molecular dynamics (receptor CRMSD [≤] 2.6 [A], retained peptide fold, [≥] 99.5% of frames preserving more than half of the initial interface contacts, and 75-82% helical content). ADMET-AI flagged the expected poor oral bioavailability of large polar peptides and no PAINS alerts. By converting single-prediction design into a cross-validated, dynamics-tested workflow, UnibindMD provides a rapid, scalable, and generalizable path from any protein target to validated peptide-binder candidates.

title: Gut microbiota in esophageal cancer: mechanisms, clinical implications, and therapeutic potential.
desc: [Frontiers in microbiology] Esophageal cancer (EC) is a highly prevalent and aggressive gastrointestinal malignancy. Late diagnosis and heterogeneous responses to chemoradiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapies severely challenge clinical management. Accumulating evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis influences esophageal mucosal malignant transformation, tumor progression, and therapeutic outcomes through the gut-esophageal axis. However, most existing research remains correlational. To bridge this gap, this review critically synthesizes the dysbiosis signatures of EC and establishes a five-tier evidence grading framework to rigorously distinguish causal mechanisms from preclinical inferences. This microbial regulation is predominantly driven by metabolite-mediated signaling, remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment (TME), intestinal barrier disruption, and oncogenic pathway activation. We functionally classify EC-associated dysbiosis into pro-tumorigenic, anti-tumorigenic, and context-dependent taxa, emphasizing a multidimensional ecosystem perspective. Furthermore, we evaluate the utility of gut microbial signatures as predictive biomarkers for neoadjuvant therapy and prognosis. Microbiota-targeted intervention strategies, including fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), microecological preparations, and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), have entered clinical exploration as adjunctive approaches to optimize treatment efficacy. Finally, we address current translational barriers and propose future directions, emphasizing multi-omics integration, spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI). This provides an objective, mechanistically grounded framework for advancing microbiota-guided personalized oncology in EC.

title: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries
desc: As wearable and digital health systems increasingly generate longitudinal physiological records, communicating these observations in patient-accessible language remains a significant challenge. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising mechanism for translating structured clinical information into readable narratives, but this process may introduce semantic drift, where clinically precise meaning is distorted during simplification. We investigate evidence-grounded health summarization for menstrual health monitoring using a constrained generation framework that combines structured evidence conditioning with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using a prompt-based constrained generation framework. We evaluate semantic alignment using Natural Language Inference (NLI), atomic factuality metrics, and readability measures. Across three LLMs and 4,500 generated summaries, explicit grounding constraints consistently improve clinical alignment, particularly by improving uncertainty preservation and, once faithfulness is evaluated against retrieved evidence, generally preserving or improving faithfulness, while effects on omission remain model-dependent. We also find that improved clinical alignment comes at the cost of increased reading difficulty and medical terminology. These findings highlight the need to jointly evaluate faithfulness, uncertainty preservation, and readability when developing patient-facing medical LLM systems.

title: Data mining of global sequence datasets markedly expands known diversity within the Tobamovirus genus
desc: High-throughput sequencing has transformed RNA virus discovery, producing vast datasets that often contain unexplored sequences of known and novel viruses across diverse sample types. Large-scale reconstruction of viral genomes within specific taxonomic groups remains a lengthy, labor-intensive process constrained by fragmented assemblies, heterogeneous workflows, and the limitations of percent identity cut-offs for taxonomic placement. Here, we focused on Tobamovirus (family Virgaviridae), a genus that contains important emerging plant pathogens. Tobamoviruses are detectable in diverse environmental matrices and are thus expected to be present across a range of datasets. We mined global short-read datasets to uncover hidden tobamovirus diversity, combining expert curation with supervised machine learning to streamline the discovery of novel tobamoviruses. Using the Serratus PalmID tool, we first identified 253 candidate datasets that are most likely to contain novel tobamoviruses. We developed a reproducible Snakemake pipeline for quality control, de novo assembly, similarity searches, and preliminary taxonomic assignment, yielding 510 candidate tobamovirus contigs across 131 datasets. Following manual curation, we confirmed 228 tobamoviral contigs from 23 datasets based on BLAST similarity searches, coding sequence content, genome organization, and assessment of potential misassemblies. To expedite the curation process, we built a two-stage machine learning classifier of tobamoviral contigs. Based on alignment-derived features and sequence properties, each ORF is first scored to determine whether it is tobamoviral. ORF-level predictions are then merged into contig-level classification using stacked generalization. Through clustering and phylogenetic analyses, we identified at least 32 putative novel tobamoviruses in datasets derived from freshwater, wastewater, plants, animal gut, and soil. Most were placed within established Tobamovirus subclades, whereas a few highly divergent sequences formed distinct basal branches related to recently identified soil-associated sequences classified as Virgaviridae sp. These findings highlight the value of aquatic and wastewater systems for expanding our understanding of tobamoviral diversity and demonstrate how data mining and targeted curation can substantially expand recognized diversity within the genus. The workflow is readily adaptable to other viral taxa and supports continuous discovery as public datasets grow

Multimodal biomarkers for early detection and immunotherapy assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma: integrating liquid biopsy, AI-based imaging and tumor immune profiling.
desc: [Frontiers in genetics] Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) commonly develops in chronically diseased liver and remains challenging because of late detection, heterogeneity, recurrence and limited hepatic reserve. Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based combinations improve outcomes in advanced HCC, but durable responses occur in only a subset of patients. This structured narrative review evaluates biomarkers by intended use: surveillance and early detection, pretreatment prognostic stratification, treatment selection, on-treatment monitoring, neoadjuvant response assessment and postoperative minimal residual disease (MRD) detection. Serum alpha-fetoprotein and clinical scores are accessible but largely reflect tumor burden, inflammation or liver function. Cell-free DNA methylation and fragmentomics provide early-detection and tissue-of-origin signals, while circulating tumor DNA tracks molecular burden and clonal evolution. Tissue and spatial profiling clarify immune responsiveness and resistance, whereas radiomics and deep learning noninvasively assess whole-tumor and peritumoral heterogeneity. These modalities are complementary but require distinct evidence standards. Most early-detection studies use case-control or enriched cohorts, and most immunotherapy associations are retrospective, prognostic or monitoring-related. No biomarker yet supports routine selection among ICI regimens. Unlike modality-specific summaries, this review aligns each biomarker with a defined clinical decision and evidentiary category and proposes a longitudinal framework integrating baseline blood, imaging and tissue features with on-treatment dynamics, preoperative reassessment and postoperative molecular surveillance. Clinical translation requires standardized assays, representative multicenter cohorts, locked external validation and biomarker-guided trials demonstrating value beyond established criteria.

title: The Value of System 1 Models in Medicine
desc: Many clinical decisions are a choice among a few fixed options, taken quickly and in large numbers. Such decisions also need an uncertainty estimate to know when to defer to a clinician. Generative language models answer slowly in free text and state their confidence poorly. In contrast, System 1 models answer zero-shot with a probability for each answer. However, their performance across clinical tasks is unknown. Four System 1 models, two proprietary and two with open weights, were evaluated zero-shot on 86 public tasks from 14 clinical domains in 20 languages, spanning examination questions and medical imaging. Tasks were assigned to six capability tiers before analysis. The primary outcome was the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC). Secondary outcomes included calibration, language effects and comparisons with published results and generative models. Across 179,111 cases, the mean AUROC of the best model per task was 0.94 for medical knowledge, 0.93 for text understanding, 0.83 for clinical judgement from text, 0.89 for image perception, 0.84 for 2D image findings and 0.69 for volumetric findings. Imaging tasks scored 0.09 (95% CI, 0.06 to 0.11) lower than text tasks (P < 0.001). The best model matched or exceeded the best published result on 13 of 26 text tasks and on 8 of 35 imaging tasks. Triage nurses outperformed the best model (accuracy, 0.85 vs. 0.56). One decision took 0.34 to 0.44 seconds and 24 to 81 joules on open-weight models run locally. Accuracy on identical questions fell by up to 39 percentage points from English to Yoruba. Generative models of the same family were 11 to 76 times slower, with 3 to 5 percentage points higher balanced accuracy. System 1 models decide quickly, cheaply and with usable confidence when the answer is stated in a text or recalled from medical knowledge, but not when it must be judged or read from an image.

title: Roche pays Zymeworks $55M for trispecific challenger to Amgen’s Imdelltra
让医疗AI基准测试更具临床可解释性-AI应用
Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Dentistry: A Scoping Review.
desc: [Australian dental journal] This review scoped artificial intelligence (AI) in paediatric dentistry to summarize current applications and limitations. A comprehensive literature search was completed across PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and medRxiv/aArXiv. The preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) checklist was used for reporting the present study. Studies concerning paediatric dentistry and utilizing AI, machine learning (ML) or large language models (LLMs) were included. Two independent reviewers screened and three extracted data on AI methodologies, performance metrics, and clinical applications. Fifty-nine studies were included. Computer vision studies (n = 32) most often used panoramic radiographs (n = 14), mainly for tooth detection, numbering and segmentation (n = 10) and caries detection (n = 9). Non-imaging ML studies (n = 18) primarily used clinical variables and questionnaire data (n = 8) or salivary/biological samples (n = 10). Accuracy ranged from 50% to 100%, with sensitivity reaching 100% in biomarker-based studies. LLM accuracy varied widely (33%-96%). Computer vision and non-imaging ML show promise for paediatric dentistry, particularly in the detection of dental structures and diseases, as well as risk stratification. Variable LLM performance underscores the need for standardized evaluation before clinical integration. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: AI-based tools may support paediatric dentists by improving tooth detection, dental structure assessment, caries detection, disease prediction and risk stratification. Computer vision and non-imaging machine learning approaches appear to have potential, but their clinical value depends on robust external validation, transparent reporting and integration into paediatric dental workflows. Given their variable performance, AI tools should be used only as adjunctive tools or a second reviewer.

title: SIM-UT: A User Simulation based Evaluation Framework for Medical Triage Chatbots
desc: LLM-based chat agents are increasingly used for complex, multi-turn, multilingual medical triage in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet evaluation methods focus on single-turn, English-only benchmarks that primarily test the chatbots' knowledge. In practice, users are often confused, overwhelmed, or emotionally vulnerable, giving unclear, misspelled single-word answers or long messages in regional dialects, and the context of a conversation can shift rapidly. We propose SIM-UT (Simulation of User Behaviour for Triage), a multi-turn, simulation-based evaluation method that identifies ecologically valid, contextually relevant failure modes of LLM-based triage chat agents. Using SIM-UT, we evaluated three real-world WhatsApp-based health chatbots: a respiratory screening programme in India, a hearing health support programme in South Africa, and a diabetes and lifestyle coaching agent in Kenya. We compared a medically fine-tuned open model (MedGemma) against general-purpose frontier models (ChatGPT and Claude) across 5,000+ multilingual simulated conversation turns grounded in the personas, constraints, and communication patterns of the real user populations, over 2-4 iterative rounds. A key failure mode emerged in both model families: de-escalation risk. The agents initially identified medical emergencies correctly, but when the user minimised the symptoms without introducing new clinical information, they de-escalated, exhibiting clinically dangerous sycophancy, for example agreeing that vaginal bleeding in pregnancy was "not a problem" or that decreased fetal movements at 32 weeks "can be normal". We recommend user simulation-based behavioural evaluation, grounded in real user context and covering adversarial and edge cases, as standard practice for triage chatbots in production, so that safeguards can be added before deployment or in subsequent iterations.

title: Gilead to pay $1.3B upfront for PepStar’s oral IL-23 challenger to J&J’s Icotyde
Artificial Intelligence in Head and Neck Reconstruction.
source: PubMed · Oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics of North America
desc: [Oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics of North America] Head and neck reconstruction is a technically demanding subspecialty where successful outcomes require precise restoration of facial form alongside masticatory and speech function. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning algorithms offer potential to expedite clinical workflows, flatten the surgical learning curve for head and neck surgeons, and enhance risk stratification of surgical patients. This article outlines the role of AI in automated image segmentation for preoperative virtual surgical planning and intraoperative guidance for perforator identification, assessment of skin paddle viability, and microvascular anastomosis safety. Applications in perioperative optimization and postoperative care of high-risk surgical patients are discussed.

title: ViBMR: A Large-Scale Multi-Sequence Brain MRI Dataset and Comprehensive Evaluation for Vietnamese Radiology Report Generation
desc: Automated radiology report generation for multi-sequence brain MRI holds strong promise for alleviating radiologists' workload, yet it remains a demanding problem: brain MRI studies are inherently volumetric, each pulse sequence carries complementary diagnostic information, and annotated data are critically scarce for low-resource clinical languages. Existing brain MRI-report resources are still dominated by English reports, translated clinical text, or datasets adapted from task-specific imaging benchmarks, leaving routine low-resource clinical reporting and heterogeneous multi-sequence MRI protocols insufficiently represented. To bridge this gap, we introduce ViBMR, to the best of our knowledge, the first large-scale multi-sequence brain MRI dataset paired with routine Vietnamese clinical reports, comprising 3,649 patients and 11,875 MRI series across T1, T2, FLAIR, and contrast-enhanced T1 sequences. Building on ViBMR, we establish a comprehensive evaluation setup for brain MRI report generation, covering representative medical vision-language models, multi-sequence inputs, and feature aggregation strategies. The results provide key insights into dataset characteristics and model behavior, while demonstrating the necessity of native low-resource clinical datasets for reliable Vietnamese-origin brain MRI report generation. Our dataset and baseline models will be released for non-commercial research.

title: Treasury sweeps biotech into proposed COINS Act restrictions, but spares Big Pharma’s China licensing deals
Enhancing learning health care systems with real-world data harmonization frameworks.
source: PubMed · ESMO real world data and digital oncology
desc: [ESMO real world data and digital oncology] The use of digital tools has enabled the capture of clinical data that can be leveraged to produce real-world evidence, complementing traditional trial data and addressing evidence gaps in oncology. Electronic health records offer rich, longitudinal data, although recording practices, collection methods, and quality may vary over time and across settings, which can lead to inconsistencies. Data harmonization is key to overcoming fragmentation, and common data models offer structured methods for unifying diverse health care data. Various mapping strategies standardize data balancing, automation, flexibility, and semantic precision: 'upstream semantic mapping' emphasizes standardization, 'downstream semantic mapping' allows tailored adjustments by local experts, and 'direct dataset mapping' focuses on creating analysis-ready datasets without intermediate data transformation. The best approach depends on organizational needs, data characteristics, and intended use cases, but harmonization must be a continuous process that adapts to evolving data sources, variable data types, new collection methods, and shifting transformation practices. Clinical expertise must ensure that cohorts mirror real-world scenarios and capture local nuances, more often with an artificial intelligence-assisted framework, while epidemiologists must consider harmonization practices in the study design and analysis. Data strategies must protect patient privacy while supporting health care improvements, with secure data handling paired with accessible sharing. By engaging medical professionals at every stage, health care institutions can become learning health systems driven by high-quality observational research, ultimately advancing knowledge and improving patient outcomes.

title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
desc: Accuracy on medical examinations is common evidence offered for the clinical use of language models, yet a health system that intends to run an open model on its own hardware needs to know considerably more: whether the model recognizes when it is likely to be wrong, whether medical fine-tuning improves this ability, whether its correct answers rest on sound clinical reasoning, or whether it actually uses the images it is given. We examine these questions for four open models of 8 to 27 billion parameters on the Spanish MIR residency examination, scoring 1,552 questions from eight editions under the exam's own rules. Answering every question, the three larger models would rank among roughly the first 600 to 3,000 candidates, with 41 to 43 specialties still open to them. Abstention, however, never pays, because even their least confident answers are right more often than the 25% break-even. Medical fine-tuning reduced overconfidence at the cost of accuracy, without improving how well confidence separates right from wrong answers. Moreover, 13-38% of correct answers rejected a distractor for a clinically unsound reason that confidence did not reflect, and removing or swapping the provided contextual images left accuracy unchanged.

title: From Blue Dye to Multimodal-Guided Surgery: The Evolution of Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping in Vulvar Cancer - A Narrative Review.
desc: [Critical reviews in oncology/hematology] The surgical management of inguinofemoral lymph nodes in early-stage vulvar cancer has progressively shifted from complete lymphadenectomy toward selective sentinel lymph node (SLN) biopsy, reducing treatment-related morbidity while preserving oncologic safety. This narrative review summarizes the historical, technical, and clinical evolution of SLN mapping, from vital blue dyes to radiotracer-based validation and contemporary multimodal image-guided approaches. A literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus was performed through May 2026, including landmark prospective studies, multicenter validation trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, and studies evaluating indocyanine green (ICG) and hybrid radioactive-fluorescent tracers. Early blue dye studies established the feasibility of lymphatic mapping, whereas technetium-99m, lymphoscintigraphy, and gamma-probe guidance provided the reproducibility required for prospective validation. GROINSS-V I supported safe omission of complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy in carefully selected SLN-negative patients, complemented by diagnostic validation in GOG-173; subsequent evidence linked SLN tumor burden to prognosis and enabled risk-adapted management of positive nodes. ICG-based near-infrared fluorescence has emerged as a valuable tool for real-time visualization and may improve intraoperative guidance. However, most comparative studies have evaluated fluorescence after radiotracer-based localization or defined the SLN according to technetium uptake, limiting conclusions regarding stand-alone interchangeability. Current evidence therefore supports ICG primarily as an adjunct within multimodal mapping rather than as a validated replacement for technetium-99m. Future progress should focus on standardized fluorescence protocols, rigorously sequenced ICG-first validation, hybrid radioactive-fluorescent strategies, and integration of imaging-derived and artificial intelligence-based tools into individualized groin management.

title: Major Revision, Minor Accountability: LLMs as Reviewers of Published Articles in Top-Tier Journals
desc: With the growth of scientific output, the peer review system is approaching a breaking point: reviewers are increasingly hard to secure, and turnaround times lengthen accordingly. LLM-assisted or LLM-generated peer review has been proposed as a remedy, but how such models would treat manuscripts already published in top-tier journals, the closest thing the current system has to a gold standard of scientific validity, is not known. Here we assembled a corpus of 200 articles, each released under a CC BY 4.0 license and published in 2026, from 20 general-science, life-science, and clinical-medicine journals including Nature, Science, and Cell, and asked four current LLMs (two proprietary, two open-weight) to produce independent peer-review reports of each one under a blinded protocol. Their decisions were overwhelmingly harsh and starkly inconsistent with each other: 605 of 800 reviews (75.6%) recommended major revision or rejection, but the rate at which any single model did so ranged from 17.5% to 100% (p < 0.001), disagreement on manuscripts that had, by construction, already survived real editorial review at the journals in question. When the same manuscripts were doctored with one deliberately planted, field-specific methodological or statistical flaw, detection rates varied from 17.0% to 60.5% across models (p < 0.001). Recommending revision for papers that had already passed editorial review (low specificity) while missing flaws deliberately placed in front of them (low sensitivity), these models produce output that should be read for what it is: an uneven, framing- and model-dependent signal.

title: Dermoscopy Explainable Intelligence Performance in Evaluating Melanoma and Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer.
desc: [Mayo Clinic proceedings] To assess the correlation between the Dermoscopy Explainable Intelligence (DEXI) score and histopathologically confirmed melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancer in a cohort of patients. This retrospective review included 178 patients who underwent total body photography by the Vectra WB360 system (Canfield Scientific Inc), sequential digital dermoscopy imaging, and subsequent biopsy of 1 or more skin lesions between May 1, 2023, and August 30, 2024. By use of an artificial intelligence-generated scoring system trained on more than 66,000 annotated dermoscopy images known as DEXI, the dermoscopy images were assigned a score from 0.0 to 10.0 calculated to assist in malignancy assessment. The histopathologically confirmed diagnosis of biopsied lesions was then compared with its associated DEXI score. Average DEXI scores by diagnosis were determined, and a clinically appropriate cut point for DEXI score was calculated. Of the 261 cases, 160 were benign with an average corresponding DEXI score of 2.5, 65 cases were non-melanoma skin cancer with an average DEXI score of 7.8, and 14 cases were melanoma with an average DEXI score of 6.0. DEXI scores from malignant lesions were statistically significantly higher than those from benign lesions. Using 3.0 as a cut point for DEXI score, we observed a sensitivity of 93.7% and a specificity of 75% in differentiating benign from malignant disease. The DEXI score was overall effective at differentiating benign from malignant disease. Larger prospective multicenter validation will be required to further evaluate for clinical use.

title: Deep Learning for Random Objects in Metric Spaces: Beyond Manifold Assumptions
desc: Deep learning (DL) methods have substantially improved predictive performance across a wide range of downstream prediction tasks, enabling new discoveries in multiple domains. However, principled DL methods for non-Euclidean random objects remain relatively scarce, despite the growing importance of modern biomedical outcomes taking the form of probability distributions, random graphs, functions, and other random objects in metric spaces. Motivated by a new generation of digital and clinical biomarkers, we propose a deep learning framework for regression with random objects in metric spaces. Our approach operates directly on the metric structure of the response space, avoiding restrictive manifold or Euclidean embedding assumptions imposed by many existing methods. At the same time, it retains modern statistical guarantees under the stated statistical assumptions. We establish statistical consistency and convergence rates for the proposed estimator, and characterize conditions under which it can mitigate the curse of dimensionality for hierarchically compositional regression functions. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate competitive predictive performance, with gains over several competing approaches in multiple Euclidean and non-Euclidean configurations. Finally, we demonstrate the practical utility of the proposed framework in two digital health case studies with distribution-valued outcomes in Wasserstein spaces, using high-resolution accelerometry and continuous glucose monitoring data. Embedding-based deep-learning methods may be less suitable when no informative low-dimensional representation exists or when the learned embedding does not adequately preserve the intrinsic geometry of the response space.

title: Comparative performance of Gemini and DeepSeek large language models in surgical decision support for mastoidectomy in chronic otitis media with cholesteatoma.
desc: [Frontiers in neurology] To compare the clinical accuracy of two state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs), Gemini Pro v3.1 and DeepSeek v3.2, in providing surgical decision support and postoperative management for mastoidectomy using expert-validated real patient data. A retrospective analysis included 121 mastoidectomy cases performed for chronic otitis media with cholesteatoma. Clinical case scenarios, including otoscopy, pure-tone audiometry, and radiological findings, were presented to both models. AI-generated responses were evaluated using a 100-point scoring system developed by four otolaryngologists in two domains: surgical planning and postoperative management. Paired-sample t-tests compared model performance, while Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis tests assessed the effects of clinical variables. No significant difference was found between Gemini and DeepSeek in surgical planning (76.07% vs. 73.97%, p = 0.258). However, Gemini significantly outperformed DeepSeek in postoperative management (67.85% vs. 62.11%, p = 0.001). Both models achieved significantly higher scores in surgical planning than postoperative care. DeepSeek demonstrated significantly higher surgical accuracy in patients with comorbidities (p = 0.004) and postoperative complications (p < 0.001). Surgical approach significantly influenced DeepSeek's performance (p = 0.001), with better results in microscopic than endoscopic cases. Both LLMs performed well in surgical planning but were less effective in postoperative management. Gemini demonstrated superior performance in postoperative recommendations, whereas DeepSeek benefited from clearer indicators of disease severity. These findings support the potential of LLMs as adjunctive tools in otologic surgical decision-making while emphasizing the need for expert clinical oversight.

title: IndoNutriQA: An Indonesian Clinical Nutrition Question Answering Benchmark
desc: Clinical Question Answering (QA) underpins Clinical Intelligent Decision Support Systems, but progress is severely limited for low-resource languages such as Indonesian by the absence of public domain-specific data. We introduce IndoNutriQA, an expert-curated Indonesian clinical QA benchmark of 911 question-answer pairs built from real clinical-nutrition reports. Rather than a large-scale training corpus, it is positioned as a high-quality evaluation resource: every pair is grounded in a clinically relevant context, enriched with structured metadata (anthropometric assessment, medical diagnosis, document provenance, chunk segmentation). Eight standardised question types following the Nutrition Care Process (NCP), including the Problem, Etiology, Sign and Symptom (PES) diagnosis statement, are answered for every report, which was written by a graduate-level dietetic intern, by one of three nutritionists. Answers are free-form clinical prose rather than extractive spans, and an expert validation study finds 6-10% of reference answers contestable. The dataset supports generative, extractive and retrieval-augmented QA as well as zero- and few-shot LLM evaluation. We report fine-tuned baselines (IndoBERT variants, mT5, RAG) with 5-fold cross-validation, learning curves and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and benchmark eight contemporary LLMs zero- and five-shot. We further calibrate our LLM-as-judge rubric against three expert raters (one RD, two nutritionists), finding it human-comparable on factuality and completeness but unreliable on clinical safety, and a human error analysis shows it misses unsupported content that the raters identify. IndoNutriQA is released to foster research in Indonesian clinical NLP and nutritional decision support.

title: Generative AI in clinical practice: how should rheumatologists evaluate and monitor emerging tools?
desc: [Arthritis care & research] Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used in rheumatology practice, to assist with tasks such as documentation, record summarization, and clinical decision support. Rheumatologists need a practical approach to determining what evidence and oversight each application requires. This narrative review proposes a framework based on two dimensions: contextual complexity and influence on patient care. Greater contextual complexity can make errors harder to detect, whereas greater influence on care increases the potential consequences of an undetected error. We examine evidence for workflow benefits and clinical effectiveness within this framework and consider safety, equity, privacy, governance, and implementation. Existing evidence on the benefits, accuracy and reliability of AI applications remains mixed. For example, studies of ambient AI scribes suggest reduced documentation burden, but evidence of improved patient outcomes from applications supporting clinical decisions is more limited. For applications with limited clinical influence, evaluation has initially focused on workflow, usability, and documentation quality. Tools that synthesize longitudinal information require additional assessment of completeness and source traceability. Those influencing diagnosis or treatment require prospective evaluation of clinical benefit and safety. Relevant vendor evidence should be assessed alongside proportionate local testing and ongoing monitoring. Safeguards should address risks such as hallucinations, automation bias, and propagating documentation errors, with attention to performance across patient groups. Changes in functionality or clinical use should prompt reassessment. The framework provides a structured basis for adoption decisions and identifies priorities for research on patient outcomes and feasible oversight in routine rheumatology care.

title: A Visual Grounding Benchmark for Retinal OCT with Multimodal Large Language Models
desc: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can answer clinical questions about medical images, but trustworthy use requires visual grounding: models should localize the pathology they report rather than rely on spurious shortcuts. Whether MLLMs can visually ground clinical findings in retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT), the most widely used imaging modality in ophthalmology, remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we introduce RetinaGroundBench, the first benchmark for biomarker visual grounding in retinal OCT. It comprises 815 B-scans exhaustively annotated by ophthalmologists with 4,537 bounding boxes covering 13 biomarkers across 8 diseases. Because MLLMs often fragment a single lesion into multiple partial predictions, we propose AggIoU, a metric that evaluates whether the union of overlapping predicted boxes covers the annotated region. Across 27 open-source MLLMs (0.8-38B parameters), we find that visual grounding remains largely unsolved: the best general-purpose model achieves a macro F1 of just 23.7%, with consistently low recall, despite reaching up to 73% balanced accuracy on biomarker presence questions. To narrow this gap, we developed RetGrounder, an MLLM fine-tuned using an OCT-specific strategy integrating grounding and textual information. Despite its relatively small size (8B), RetGrounder improves grounding F1 to 33.9%, a 43% relative improvement. Our benchmark provides a reference point for measuring progress in the field of OCT diagnosis with MLLMs.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Digital Consultant: Evaluating Large Language Models for Patient Inquiries on Dental Caries.
source: PubMed · Journal of esthetic and restorative dentistry : official publication of the American Academy of Esthetic Dentistry ... [et al.]
desc: [Journal of esthetic and restorative dentistry : official publication of the American Academy of Esthetic Dentistry ... [et al.]] To evaluate the clinical accuracy, usefulness, global overall quality (GQS), and readability of ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek responses to patient questions regarding dental caries. Fifty-nine simulated patient questions concerning caries diagnosis, etiology, treatment, and prevention were queried in Turkish. Three restorative dentists independently evaluated the responses for accuracy, usefulness, and GQS. Readability was assessed using the Ateşman index. Statistical analyses included the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for interrater reliability, the Friedman test for performance comparisons among the models, and Spearman's rank correlation to analyze the relationships between the clinical variables. Inter-rater reliability was high across all criteria (ICC > 0.75). Significant performance differences existed among the models (p < 0.001); Gemini achieved the highest overall clinical accuracy, usefulness, and GQS scores. ChatGPT produced the most readable texts, categorized generally as "easy to read" according to the Ateşman index. For DeepSeek, higher clinical accuracy significantly correlated with better readability (p < 0.001). Gemini offers the highest accuracy and quality as a digital preconsultation tool. However, AI tools should complement, not replace, professional dental advice.

title: nnInteractive Agent: General-Purpose AI Agents as 3D Image Annotators
desc: Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it. General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. We show that such agents can take over this work without additional training: the user makes a request in plain language, and the agent works out what has to be segmented, locates the targets, prompts nnInteractive, inspects the 3D result, corrects it and responds to feedback. Asked for 'the muscles used for chewing', an agent identifies and segments the masseters and pterygoids; asked to count liver lesions, it writes its own code to find candidates and splits a merged lesion on request. Our open-source nninteractive-agent provides nnInteractive as tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it. On a benchmark spanning CT, MRI, PET and micro-CT of humans, a mouse and an ant (14 images; 51 targets from organs and tumours to muscles, foot bones, vessel trees and an insect brain), Claude Code and Codex reach a mean Dice of 0.81 and 0.84 from the request alone; when told where each target is, both reach 0.85 and prompt nearly as effectively as an oracle that places prompts using the reference segmentation. A text-prompted 3D model (VoxTell) is more accurate on most standard radiological targets but less robust: it returns an empty mask for one of them and fails on the leg muscles, the foot bones, the mouse and the ant, where the agents remain accurate. Code: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nninteractive-agent

title: Dynamic control of carbon-ion radiation dose distribution amid respiratory motion challenges: A review of prediction research using geant4 and deep learning physics-constrained models.
source: PubMed · Journal of applied clinical medical physics
desc: [Journal of applied clinical medical physics] Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) offers superior dose conformity and biological effectiveness; however, its precision is highly sensitive to respiratory motion, leading to dose uncertainty and interplay effects that compromise treatment accuracy. A comprehensive literature synthesis was conducted on studies employing motion-resolved imaging techniques (e.g. SMEIR), dynamic dose prediction, 4D robust planning, and hybrid adaptive methods for CIRT. The study emphasised the use of Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations combined with deep learning models, including physics-informed neural networks, to simulate and predict dose perturbations caused by respiratory motion. This review also examined clinical treatment planning systems, radiobiological modelling, and adaptive strategies to mitigate the effects of motion. The integration of Geant4 with deep learning enabled high-fidelity, computationally efficient dose prediction under respiratory motion, improving accuracy in dose localization and adaptation. Motion management techniques such as respiratory gating, rescanning, and 4D robust optimization demonstrated enhanced tumor control and normal tissue sparing. Hybrid models combining Monte Carlo data and AI inference show promise for near-real-time adaptive therapy. Despite these advances, challenges remain, including limited motion-rich datasets, computational demands for real-time recalculations, and the complexity of incorporating variable relative biological effectiveness (RBE) into adaptive planning. Combining Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulations with deep learning frameworks shows emerging promise for controlling carbon ion dose distributions amid respiratory motion, though direct clinical validation for this combination remains limited. These hybrid models may enhance the precision and adaptability of CIRT, offering improved outcomes. Future efforts should focus on clinical validation, standardization, and overcoming computational and data limitations to facilitate clinical translation of motion-adaptive CIRT. These approaches remain at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL 3-5) and require prospective clinical validation before routine implementation.

title: Diagnostic Loss: Asymmetric Supervision for Radiology Report Generation
desc: Automated radiology report generation requires models to do more than produce fluent clinical narratives: they must explicitly state supported diagnoses while avoiding unsupported ones. However, existing medical vision-language models (MedVLMs) are typically trained with token-level maximum likelihood objectives, which prioritize text agreement over diagnostically critical terms. As a result, models can miss key diagnoses and introduce wrong ones. We identify this as an objective misalignment between conventional language modeling and the asymmetric diagnostic requirements of radiology reporting. To encode these requirements, we introduce Diagnostic Loss (DLoss), a differentiable, architecture-agnostic objective that operates directly on decoder token probabilities. DLoss separately aggregates probability mass over vocabularies associated with diagnoses supported by the reference report and with unsupported alternatives. Using asymmetric pooling across token positions in the report, it encourages supported diagnoses to receive sufficient probability in at least one position while suppressing spurious probability spikes for unsupported diagnoses across all positions during training. The loss can be applied to existing 3D MedVLMs without modifying their vision backbones, language decoders, or inference procedures, and introduces no additional inference-time computation. We train and evaluate DLoss on 50,000 abdominal CT scans across several 3D MedVLM architectures on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution report-generation benchmarks. Across these settings, DLoss improves diagnostic faithfulness while maintaining competitive performance on conventional language-generation metrics, showing the value of asymmetric sequence-level supervision for radiology report generation. The code for DLoss is available at https://github.com/gmum/DLoss.

title: Artificial intelligence for facial soft-tissue landmark localization, measurement, and classification in orthodontics: A systematic review.
source: PubMed · European journal of oral sciences
desc: [European journal of oral sciences] This systematic review provides a broad overview of three distinct applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in facial soft-tissue assessment: landmark localization, automated facial measurement, and classification of soft-tissue conditions in orthodontic and dentofacial evaluation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, ClinicalTrials.gov, Google Scholar, and Open Science Framework were searched. Studies using 2D facial photographs, 3D facial scans, or AI-generated facial models were included. Risk of bias was assessed with an adapted QUADAS-2 tool and certainty of evidence with GRADE. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261452521). Fifteen studies were included. Landmark-localization performance varied substantially by imaging modality, landmark definition, data set, reference standard, and error metric; central and anatomically well-defined landmarks were generally more accurate than peripheral or subjective points. Agreement for AI-derived measurements ranged from poor to excellent, with ICCs of approximately 0.01-0.984. Classification accuracy ranged from approximately 0.83 to 0.98, with AUCs up to 0.98. Given only two narrowly scoped classification studies, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than broadly generalizable. Because of substantial methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized qualitatively. Current evidence supports AI as an adjunctive tool, but routine clinical implementation requires robust external validation and clinician oversight. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261452521.

title: GWDM: A Guided Wavelet Diffusion Model for Realistic Histopathology Image Generation
desc: Histopathology images are recognized as a reliable and comprehensive modality for Deep Learning (DL) based diagnosis. However, effectiveness is constrained by limited large-scale annotated datasets, as collecting expert-labeled medical data is costly and time-intensive. Recent advances in generative models, particularly diffusion models, demonstrate strong capabilities in synthesizing medically relevant content for dataset augmentation. Existing generative frameworks treat histopathology patches as generic natural images, failing to enforce biological constraints such as histomorphological structures and heterogeneous staining patterns essential for valid synthesis. We propose a guided wavelet diffusion model (GWDM) framework that captures image details at multiple scales using wavelets and leverages controllable conditioning based on domain-specific histopathological features (e.g., tissue patterns and color variations). We further formulate a histomorphological guidance loss applied to real and generated patches. A loss ramping strategy gradually introduces these constraints during training, ensuring stable optimization and robust modeling of tissue architecture. GWDM was evaluated on three benchmark datasets (BCSS, MoNuSeg, and PAIP2019), consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative methods. Ablation studies confirmed that domain-guided conditioning, perceptual loss, and structural similarity loss each contribute meaningfully to synthesis quality. Downstream nuclei and tissue segmentation experiments further validated the clinical utility of GWDM-generated images, demonstrating consistent performance improvements when synthetic data augments real training sets. This work shows that domain-specific conditioning and dual-loss optimization generate realistic histopathology patches, reducing data scarcity and improving clinical downstream segmentation performance.

title: Multi-parameter optimization of recombinant protein secretion in Bacillus subtilis: a review.
desc: [Microbial cell factories] Bacillus subtilis is widely recognized as one of the most robust and versatile hosts for recombinant protein production. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the protein secretion pathway in B. subtilis, detailing its mechanistic basis and key limiting steps. We discuss the structural features of signal peptides (SPs) that govern efficient translocation and highlight recent advances in de novo promoter and signal peptide engineering. A particular focus is placed on the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) to predict and design optimal genetic elements. Drawing on findings from combinatorial and multi-parameter studies, we propose that future engineering strategies should move beyond maximizing individual parameters. Instead, achieving a dynamic balance across transcriptional, translational and secretion layers is essential to sustain high productivity while minimizing cellular secretion stress. This review offers a roadmap for systems-level engineering of B. subtilis as a next-generation protein production platform.

title: Large language models show systematic failures in incorporating evolving medical knowledge
desc: Medical knowledge evolves as clinical guidelines revise recommendations, yet whether large language models (LLMs) faithfully incorporate such changes remains unclear. We introduce ChronoEvo, comprising 1,709 recommendation-level revisions across 12 forms of medical knowledge change, to distinguish recognition of revised guidance from incorporation into clinical recommendations. In the primary model, 90.8% of responses recognized revisions and 80.2% were clinically correct, but only 58.5% fully incorporated guidance, yielding a 32.3-percentage-point recognition-incorporation gap. This dissociation persisted across 14 models and was corroborated by two clinicians' adjudicated assessment of 300 responses, yielding a 40.3-percentage-point gap in the validation sample. Changes in recommendation strength and patient eligibility were associated with retention of outdated guidance. A revision-salience intervention reduced outdated-content retention and improved clinical correctness but did not significantly improve full incorporation.
