These findings identify faithful incorporation of evolving medical knowledge as a distinct challenge for clinical LLM reliability, even when updated guideline evidence is available.

title: From validation to public health impact: implementing equitable AI-enabled diabetic retinopathy screening.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a preventable cause of vision loss as diabetes prevalence rises worldwide. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled retinal screening has progressed from retrospective validation to prospective and real-world deployment, with recent reviews showing high diagnostic performance across fundus photography, smartphone-based systems, and autonomous platforms. Yet diagnostic accuracy alone does not ensure public health benefit. Population impact can be lost when eligible people are not reached, images are ungradable, results are delayed, referrals are incomplete, treatment capacity is insufficient, or disadvantaged groups face financial, geographic, or digital barriers. Unlike reviews centered mainly on diagnostic accuracy or economic performance, this Mini Review reframes AI-enabled DR screening as a population-health intervention spanning detection through completion of effective eye care. We synthesize evidence on diagnostic validity, implementation, economics, referral completion, care cascades, patient-centered outcomes, equity, and governance. We argue that effectiveness and cost-effectiveness are properties of the complete screening-to-treatment pathway, not the algorithm alone, and propose a four-domain framework encompassing technical validity, service integration, population impact, and equity and sustainability. Future research should prioritize comparative implementation studies and outcome sets that capture screening reach, gradability, referral completion, treatment initiation, time to treatment, avoidable vision loss, vision-related quality of life, acceptability, costs, and subgroup equity. The policy question is no longer whether AI can detect DR, but whether health systems can translate automated detection into equitable completion of effective eye care at scale.

title: Evaluating Type-1 Diabetes Digital Twins by Decision Quality
desc: A digital twin (DT) for type 1 diabetes (T1D) can predict how an individual's blood glucose will respond to different insulin treatments without actually trying them. For each treatment, downstream statistics of predicted glucose trajectories, such as glycemic risk, can be computed to guide clinical decisions. However, the quality of DTs is usually measured by the accuracy of their predicted glucose trajectories, which may not reflect the quality of the downstream treatment decisions they inform. In this work, we directly evaluate DTs by this decision quality on downstream treatment ranking, i.e., whether a DT predicts glucose trajectories that can be used to rank candidate treatments as the real patient would. We present an evaluation protocol over 30 virtual patients from the FDA-accepted UVA/Padova model, each simulated under 21 different basal-bolus treatments. For each patient, a DT is fitted under one treatment and then produces glucose trajectories for the remaining 20 treatments. Our results show that prediction accuracy and decision quality disagree. A baseline that models the average patient, never seeing the individual's glucose data, has the lowest prediction accuracy of all six methods (RMSE: 63.6 mg/dL) but ranks treatments with the second-highest mean Spearman (0.766), while a black-box neural network that predicts glucose nearly twice as accurately (RMSE: 32.9 mg/dL) ranks them no better than a random ordering of the 20 treatments (0.049 Spearman). Therefore, selecting a DT based on prediction accuracy alone can prefer one that recommends treatments at chance, and decision quality must be evaluated directly rather than assumed to follow from prediction accuracy.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmacy Services: A Comparative Bibliometric Analysis of United States and Global Research Trends.
desc: [Journal of patient safety] Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies offer transformative potential to address pharmacy workforce challenges and enhance patient safety. This study aimed to characterize the global landscape of AI research in pharmacy services and identify gaps between research activity and patient safety priorities. A bibliometric analysis was conducted on AI-pharmacy services publications indexed in Web of Science (2015-2025). Performance analysis and science mapping techniques were applied using Bibliometrix software to compare United States and non-U.S. research output, thematic evolution, and collaboration patterns. A total of 4426 documents met inclusion criteria, comprising 1619 (36.58%) United States and 2807 (63.42%) non-U.S. publications. Both corpora exhibited exponential growth. The United States contributed 29.30% of global output with higher international coauthorship rates (35.08% versus 19.91%). Thematic mapping identified "prediction" and "risk" as motor themes in U.S. research. However, co-word analysis revealed a significant translational gap: critical patient safety themes-medication error prevention and workflow optimization-were conspicuously underrepresented. Neither "medication error" nor "patient safety" appeared among high-frequency keywords despite substantial clinical relevance. Current AI-pharmacy research prioritizes algorithmic development over patient safety implementation. Strategic realignment toward medication error prevention and safety-focused applications is warranted to realize AI's potential in enhancing pharmaceutical care quality.

title: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Label-Efficient Gastric Cancer Detection and Intra-Tumour Progression Analysis
desc: Gastric Cancer is among the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The complexity and variability of histopathological images pose significant challenges for both pathologists and computer-based diagnostics, creating a growing need for machine learning approaches capable of capturing meaningful representations from limited labelled data. Selfsupervised Contrastive Learning (CL) has demonstrated promising results in natural image analysis; however, its application to gastric cancer histopathology remains underexplored. This paper proposes an integrated CL framework built on a ResNet50 encoder trained under the NT-Xent objective, without reliance on ImageNet pre-training, to learn discriminative and staining-invariant representations from H&E-stained tissue patches. The learned embeddings are transferred to a supervised downstream classifier for binary tumour/normal (TUM/NOR) detection, achieving a test accuracy of 83.13%, an AUC-ROC of 0.9087, and an Average Precision of 0.9063 - competitive with recent supervised and weakly-supervised approaches on comparable histopathology benchmarks. Beyond binary diagnosis, the framework applies K-Means clustering to tumour embeddings to identify four geometrically separable pseudo-stage clusters, confirmed by a Random Forest classifier achieving 97% accuracy and a mean Dice coefficient of 0.97, demonstrating the capacity of CL representations to encode progression-relevant morphological variation without stage-level annotations. Grad-CAM explainability is integrated throughout to ensure model transparency. The complete system is deployed via a Streamlit clinical interface. Compared to recent state-of-the-art methods the proposed framework operates with substantially fewer labelled samples while additionally providing unsupervised progression stratification and interpretable outputs, addressing a gap not covered by existing approaches.

title: Endometrial cancer molecular classification: research advances and clinical application.
desc: [Frontiers in oncology] As research in molecular biology continues to advance, the classification of endometrial cancer has gradually shifted from traditional histology toward risk stratification based on the integration of molecular subtyping with clinicopathologic factors. Molecular subtyping has not only transformed our understanding of the biological heterogeneity of endometrial cancer but also provided new evidence for prognostic assessment and treatment selection. However, the maturity of clinical evidence and the translational therapeutic value vary across molecular subtypes. This review systematically summarizes the molecular characteristics and clinical significance of the POLE ultramutated(POLE-mut)subtype, mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) subtype, p53 abnormal (p53-abn) subtype, and no specific molecular profile (NSMP) subtype, with a focus on evaluating whether different molecular features can be further translated from risk stratification into specific treatment decisions. Centering on key issues such as de-escalated therapy for the POLE-mut subtype, the predictive value of immunotherapy for the dMMR subtype, intensified therapy for the p53-abn subtype, and further risk stratification of the NSMP subtype, this review analyzes the clinical basis and limitations of existing evidence and further discusses the challenges that tumors with multiple molecular features pose for classification and treatment decision making. Building on this, the paper compares how major international guidelines integrate molecular information with clinical and pathologic factors and analyzes real world implementation barriers such as testing standardization, result interpretation, and healthcare accessibility. Finally, it outlines the potential value of emerging technologies, including liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence, and multiomics, in dynamic risk assessment and precision therapy. This review aims to trace the continuum of evidence from molecular discovery to clinical action, clarifying which clinical decisions can be supported by existing molecular markers and identifying questions that current evidence cannot yet answer, thereby providing guidance for the precise application and clinical translation of molecular subtyping in endometrial cancer.

title: LACToS: Local Anomaly Detection via Conditional Typicality of Superpixels
desc: Local anomaly detection is the task of identifying spatially confined anomalous or out-of-distribution (OOD) regions within an otherwise in-distribution (ID) image. Most existing methods are designed for a specific context, with a strong focus on industrial defect detection, where they achieve excellent performance on well-established benchmarks. However, we observe that these methods can exhibit significant performance drops in other contexts, especially when the inlier distribution is multimodal. To account for this inlier complexity, we propose LACToS, a principled local OOD detection method based on statistical typicality and made tractable through two innovations: (i) grouping pixels into superpixels and (ii) using a computationally efficient proxy to estimate typicality. We evaluate LACToS across three diverse applications spanning medical imaging, human faces, and X-ray security screening. LACToS performs more robustly than prior methods across these benchmarks. The code is released here: https://github.com/voilalab/LACToS.

title: Artificial intelligence and biotechnology for smart storage: Quality and safety perspectives in horticultural produce.
source: PubMed · Current research in food science
desc: [Current research in food science] Addressing the global challenge of postharvest losses in horticultural produce requires the continuous development of innovative strategies that integrate cutting-edge technology with fundamental biological knowledge. This review explores the synergy between artificial intelligence (AI), biotechnology, and traditional postharvest management strategies to improve the quality, safety, and shelf-life of fruits and vegetables (F&V). We examine the physiological and molecular mechanisms driving postharvest deterioration, including respiration, senescence, and host-pathogen interactions, while evaluating how AI-driven tools are advancing quality monitoring, predictive analytics, and supply chain optimization. Furthermore, we assess the potential of advanced biotechnological interventions, such as CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing and RNA interference techniques, to extend shelf-life and enhance the disease resistance in horticultural crops. By evaluating recent progress in these domains, we present integrated strategies that combine biological insight with digital transformation for sustainable postharvest management. The effective implementation of these approaches holds considerable potential to reduce F&V waste, enhance food security, and create horticultural supply chains that are more resilient to ever growing global production and evolving environmental challenges.

title: RetiJev: Fast and Source-Grounded Ophthalmic Decision Models
desc: Ophthalmic clinical decision support requires fast, accurate, and privacy-preserving inference, yet autoregressive large language models (LLMs) incur substantial latency and computational overhead for decisions among predefined actions. We therefore investigate a decision-oriented alternative to generative reasoning. Specifically, we first introduce RetiJev-Data, a source-grounded ophthalmology corpus comprising 78,158 clinical-decision and diagnosis questions derived from articles in PubMed Central and a MeSH vocabulary covering 531 eye diseases, and 50,074 guideline-grading questions spanning 11 grading systems, along with a 24,662-question evaluation benchmark. Based on this, we develop RetiJev, a family of 0.8B-9B decision models that directly score candidate answers without autoregressive decoding. Across all model sizes, RetiJev outperforms both a 27B LLM and the commercial Jev 1.13 decision model on guideline grading by 10.4-23.0 points. RetiJev-9B further achieves the highest accuracy on clinical decisions, improving over both baselines by 5.4-6.5 points while matching them on diagnosis. It answers a case in 158 ms on one GPU, 3.5x faster than LLM generation and 470x faster than reasoning. Models are released at https://github.com/Awenbocc/RetiJev.

title: Building smarter surveillance: a framework for artificial intelligence-enabled monitoring of overuse injuries in youth sports.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] Early sport specialization (ESS), defined as intensive, year-round training in a single sport at the exclusion of others, has become increasingly prevalent among youth athletes. This trend has coincided with a rise in overuse injuries, and premature attrition. Concurrently, advances in wearable sensors and artificial intelligence (AI) enable real-time quantification of training load, biomechanical deviations, and recovery. However, a translational gap remains: existing AI surveillance models are predominantly validated in elite adult male cohorts, leaving youth athletes underserved. To address this gap, we propose a translational four-pillar framework for ESS-aware AI injury monitoring in youth sport. Bridging technological capabilities with developmental physiology through structured AI surveillance provides a structured risk-monitoring roadmap with the potential to inform preventative strategies, optimize physical readiness, and support long-term musculoskeletal health in youth athletes.

title: ICGF-CXRMate: Image-Conditioned Clinical Context Compression and Gated Fusion for Chest X-ray Report Generation
desc: Auxiliary patient data can improve chest X-ray report generation, but directly concatenating heterogeneous clinical information with visual tokens produces long, variable-length decoder prompts and may expose the model to redundant or image-irrelevant context. We propose ICGF-CXRMate, an image-conditioned clinical context compression and gated fusion framework. Learnable queries are first conditioned on the current chest X-ray representations and then attend to the patient-data sequence, compressing it into a fixed number of clinical context tokens. Gated cross-attention selectively integrates these tokens into the visual stream, while the compressed tokens are retained in the decoder prompt as a direct clinical pathway. Experiments on linked MIMIC-CXR and MIMIC-IV-ED examinations show that ICGF-CXRMate improves report quality while reducing the average prompt length. In Stage~2, it improves RadGraph-F1 from 24.00 to 28.86, CXR-BERT similarity from 56.86 to 62.80, and BLEU-4 from 5.14 to 7.96 compared with CXRMate-ED, while reducing the average prompt length from 373.89 to 288.37 tokens, corresponding to a 22.9\% reduction. After self-critical sequence training, ICGF-CXRMate outperforms CXRMate-ED on six of eight report-quality metrics in Stage~3. Ablation studies confirm the complementary contributions of image-conditioned compression, gated fusion, and direct retention of the compressed clinical tokens.

title: Recurrent implantation failure: a registry-corroborated, age-stratified definition and pragmatic five-tiered management algorithm.
desc: [Frontiers in endocrinology] Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remains a significant challenge in reproductive medicine, imposing substantial emotional, clinical, and financial burden on affected couples. RIF is generally defined as failure to achieve pregnancy after multiple transfers of good-quality embryos, yet progress in the field has been constrained by the absence of a universally accepted definition and by the inherent complexity of investigating the embryo-endometrial interface. Recent evidence has prompted a reappraisal of the factors contributing to RIF, distinguishing it from the mechanistically distinct entity of embryo-intrinsic failure (recurrent embryo arrest and poor embryo development). This narrative review synthesises epidemiological data, evaluates the evidence base for available diagnostic modalities, and appraises current management strategies, including the controversies surrounding adjunctive treatments. We propose a registry-corroborated, age-stratified definition of RIF - the ABCDE framework - and a five-tiered, clinically applicable management algorithm that integrates the available evidence with expert recommendation to guide clinicians within a shared decision-making framework. Future directions include prospective multicentre validation, incorporation of artificial intelligence for risk prediction, and development of novel therapeutic approaches targeting the embryo-endometrial interface.

title: Better Reasoning, Not Just Bigger Models: A Structure-Grounded Framework for Efficient and Reliable Inference
desc: Scaling large language models has substantially improved linguistic fluency, yet reliable autonomous agents require more than fluent generation. In multi-turn inference, current agentic systems often produce semantically plausible but structurally ungrounded reasoning, especially under incomplete observations. We propose Structure-Grounded Uncertainty Reduction (SGUR), a training-free framework that complements token-level generation with active uncertainty reduction over structured hypothesis spaces. SGUR represents incomplete observations as a query graph and aligns them with candidate hypothesis graphs through a prior-weighted partial graph matching mechanism, where database-derived empirical priors assign greater importance to decision-relevant relations rather than treating all graph edges uniformly. The resulting inference state is iteratively refined by an active information-gain strategy that selects the next most informative node to query, systematically pruning the candidate space. We instantiate SGUR on a challenging PrimeKG-derived sequential medical diagnosis benchmark, demonstrating that structural grounding can partially substitute for model scale: starting from only two observed symptoms, SGUR achieves 92.5% Hit@3, outperforming the strongest Graph-RAG baseline by 9.4 percentage points while using approximately 5x fewer tokens. Notably, SGUR enables smaller backbone models to match or exceed the performance of models up to 10x larger, suggesting that structural grounding provides a more robust and efficient paradigm for scaling agent performance than relying exclusively on increasing model size.

title: Physics-aware geometric deep learning for pre-planning dosimetric feasibility in Gamma Knife radiosurgery.
desc: [Radiological physics and technology] In Gamma Knife stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), achieving optimal dosimetric outcomes is physically constrained by complex tumor geometry. While the Gradient Index (GI) and Conformity Index (CI) define plan quality, the volume receiving [Formula: see text] and Shot Density dictate patient safety and efficiency. Current volumetric heuristics fail to capture the topological irregularities that govern these parameters. This study introduces a physics-aware Geometric Deep Learning framework to simultaneously predict quality, safety, and complexity metrics directly from surface topology. Methods: Utilizing the Vestibular-Schwannoma-SEG dataset [Formula: see text], tumor manifolds were converted into physics-aware point clouds enriched with 12-dimensional feature vectors, including surface normals and radial curvature. A multi-task PointNet-based architecture, termed "GammaPoint-Net," was developed to regress GI, CI, [Formula: see text], and Shot Density. The framework was benchmarked against 3D Voxel-based CNNs, standard volumetric regression, conventional machine-learning regressors trained on handcrafted 3D shape descriptors (Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, and XGBoost), and point-based architectures using 5-fold cross-validation. GammaPoint-Net achieved superior predictive accuracy across all objectives ([Formula: see text]), significantly outperforming volumetric baselines [Formula: see text]. Ablation studies confirmed that incorporating differential geometric features reduced the mean absolute error by 46%. GammaPoint-Net also outperformed the strongest handcrafted shape-descriptor baseline (XGBoost augmented with curvature moments, [Formula: see text]; paired Wilcoxon [Formula: see text] ). Saliency mapping demonstrated that the network autonomously identifies high-curvature surface protrusions as the primary drivers of dosimetric degradation. GammaPoint-Net demonstrates that surface topology, rather than volume, is the fundamental determinant of radiosurgical plan quality. This framework provides an instantaneous, interpretable pre-planning assessment, enabling physicists to anticipate plan difficulty and toxicity risks prior to optimization.

title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
desc: Modern LLM agents can retrieve information from accessible documents, and then disclose a sensitive conclusion assembled from them. This mosaic effect creates a critical risk for agents operating over confidential data. We quantify its realization with 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military examples, yielding 10,800 final answers from three LLM agents in controlled simulation and 1,440 answers from live agents in two open-source harnesses. Even under benign queries designed to be answerable from one document, GPT-5.6-Sol, the best performing model tested, discloses forbidden composites in 7.08% of answers (95% CI: 3.75-10.67%) in simulation, with worse disclosure rates in live harnesses. Adding visible classification headers and explicit aggregation rules reduces pooled disclosure rates substantially, yet unsafe disclosures persist in 32.37% of simulated answers (95% CI: 28.33-36.19%) across all intents despite these safeguards. Furthermore, increased refusals do not guarantee confidentiality, since significant refusals reveal the prohibited conclusion regardless. These results point to a troubling conclusion: sensitive data leaks via mosaic-style events are an observed confidentiality failure mode in the evaluated settings at non-negligible rates. They motivate stronger controls on what agents may infer and disclose in sensitive data environments with mixed-clearance users.

title: In Situ Ion-Exchange-Mediated Dynamic Nanointerface Reconfiguration for Polarity-Switchable Photoelectrochemical-Photothermal Biosensing.
source: PubMed · Journal of the American Chemical Society
desc: [Journal of the American Chemical Society] Conventional photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems typically rely on static semiconductor interfaces that merely translate biomolecular recognition into amplitude modulation of the pre-existing photocurrent, thus limiting their analytical robustness and self-validation capabilities. Herein, we report in situ ion-exchange-mediated dynamic nanointerface engineering to fabricate an analyte-programmed reconfigurable PEC-photothermal (PT) dual-mode biosensor for the carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) assay. The Z-scheme heterostructure of a plasmonic Au nanoparticle (NP) layer-supported BiOI/AgI/indium tin oxide glass (BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO) is constructed as the initial photoelectrode. In the sensing process, a CEA recognition event directly reshapes the phase composition of BiOI/AgI, charge-transfer behavior, and photoresponse polarity. The synergistic integration of the BiOI/AgI heterostructure and the close-packed layer of plasmonic Au NPs substantially enhance the light absorption, charge separation, and interfacial charge transfer, making BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO a highly suitable photoelectrode for the PEC mode of the PEC-PT biosensor. This analyte-driven phase evolution reconstructs the semiconductor composition, band alignment, and charge-transfer pathways to switch the photocurrent polarity from cathodic to anodic. In addition, a photothermal imaging mode of the PEC-PT biosensor is triggered by regulating the Bi2S3 formation for intrinsic cross-validation. By integrating an artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted analysis, PEC-PT biosensors enable robust multimodal quantification and improved analytical reliability, achieving > 99.8% prediction accuracy in real-sample analysis. This is the first example of integrating a dynamic nanointerface-driven PEC-PT dual-mode biosensor with artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced multimodal analysis for CEA detection and provides a dynamic nanointerface-driven strategy for intelligent multimode biosensing.

title: SciFusion: Physics-Guided Compositional Diffusion for Multimodal 3D Scientific Image Generation
desc: Existing 3D generative approaches are typically developed for individual imaging modalities, requiring substantial modality-specific data and limiting their ability to exploit shared structure across scientific imaging domains. We present SciFusion, a multimodal framework for unified 3D scientific image generation built on a latent diffusion backbone, with two key contributions. First, we introduce a compositional conditioning scheme that factorizes each modality into domain, object, and contrast representations. Sharing these factors across related modalities enables knowledge transfer across heterogeneous imaging domains and allows the factors to be recombined at inference time to synthesize unseen domain-object-contrast compositions in a zero-shot manner. Second, we incorporate domain-specific physics-informed objectives: Fourier spectral consistency for MRI, Radon projection consistency for CT, and multislice diffraction consistency for electron microscopy, to encourage generated samples to respect modality-dependent image formation processes. Extensive experiments across 15 medical and scientific imaging modalities demonstrate that SciFusion improves generation fidelity and cross-domain generalization over modality-specific and flattened multimodal conditioning strategies, while enabling zero-shot synthesis of unseen compositions without training on those target compositions. These results demonstrate that compositional, physics-guided conditioning provides a scalable framework for unified 3D scientific image generation, particularly for emerging modalities where large-scale training data are difficult to obtain.

title: Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.
desc: [Molecular and biochemical parasitology] Veterinary parasitic diseases remain a major threat to livestock production, companion animal health, wildlife conservation, and public health worldwide. Conventional diagnostic methods, including microscopy, serology, and culture-based techniques, often suffer from limited sensitivity, poor specificity, prolonged turnaround time, and dependence on specialized laboratory facilities. Recent advances in Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-based diagnostics have introduced highly sensitive, rapid, and field-deployable platforms for parasite detection. This review critically summarizes the principles and recent applications of CRISPR/Cas12, Cas13, and emerging Cas14-based diagnostic approaches in veterinary parasitology, covering protozoan, helminthic, and arthropod-borne parasites. It further compares CRISPR platforms and discusses their integration with isothermal amplification, lateral flow assays, fluorescence detection, and portable biosensors to improve diagnostic performance. Moreover, current challenges, including sample preparation, assay standardization, multiplex detection, regulatory approval, and commercialization, are highlighted. Finally, future perspectives on amplification-free CRISPR assays, artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, and point-of-care platforms are discussed. By providing a translational perspective from laboratory innovation to field application, this review highlights the potential of CRISPR-based diagnostics to transform veterinary parasite surveillance and disease control.

title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
desc: Despite recent advances, current AI systems remain highly susceptible to domain shifts, particularly in biomedical imaging, where images are usually acquired under substantially different experimental conditions. Although recent domain adaptation methods have made substantial progress, significant performance gaps under domain shift persist. To measure progress in this regard, we introduce BatchBench, a leaderboard that evaluates and compares the robustness of AI systems on biomedical images from unseen experimental batches and data sources. BatchBench is built on JUMP-CP, one of the largest publicly available biomedical imaging datasets. Generated using the Cell Painting assay, JUMP-CP exhibits pronounced batch effects and domain shifts, making it a challenging testbed for evaluating robustness to distributional changes.

title: Scentronic: An artificial intelligence-assisted olfactory interface for remote odor sharing and transmission.
desc: [Science advances] Recent years have witnessed the surge of human-machine interfaces (HMIs) for various applications. Olfaction is a fundamental chemical sense crucial to perception, memory, and emotion. Current limitations arise from the difficulty of accurately capturing, transmitting, and reproducing odor signals, and the lack of standardized, network-enabled platforms. This work presents an internet of things (IoT)-enabled olfactory interface for remote odor sensing and stimulation. The system integrates an artificial intelligence-assisted odor sensing platform with a wearable piezoelectric olfactory actuation system. We demonstrate the design, characterization, and application of this framework, which integrates devices, circuit architecture, and software algorithms. Applications in medical contexts include psychophysical testing to study olfactory pathways and evaluate sensory loss. We further showcase multisensory stimulation through integrated olfactory and gustatory interfaces for enhanced immersion. This study establishes a scalable framework for IoT-based olfactory interaction, advancing HMIs toward a future that includes the long-overlooked chemical senses.

title: Expandable Modality Experts for Medical Vision-Language Learning
desc: Learning across medical imaging modalities requires making use of images without paired text and accommodating new domains while retaining existing representations. We propose a medical vision-language technique built around an expandable bank of modality experts. Its Multiway Transformer combines shared visual computation with deterministically routed feed-forward experts and a separate text pathway. A modality-aware visual tokenizer supplies targets for masked pretraining on 19.4 million unpaired image rows across seven modalities; contrastive alignment then uses 3.23 million image-text pairs. Additional fundus and optical coherence tomography experts learn from paired data while the original image and text embedding paths remain frozen. With a ViT-Large backbone, the proposed technique achieves the best or tied-best result in 24 of 25 benchmark settings across nine modalities: 10 of 11 zero-shot classification benchmarks, all 10 linear probes, and all four retrieval benchmarks. Mean balanced accuracy is 0.674 for zero-shot classification and 0.856 for linear probing, and mean bidirectional retrieval recall is 20.70%. A separate three-seed sequential experiment with matched adaptation data yields fundus and OCT retrieval gains of 14.95 and 9.31 percentage points, with no measured loss on preceding fundus or pathology tasks. The preservation argument requires unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions, and feature-identity checks verify retention on evaluated inputs. The proposed technique provides a modular approach to learning and expanding medical vision-language representations.

title: The AI debate is missing half the system.
desc: [Science (New York, N.Y.)] Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human-AI system, not the AI model alone.

title: Revealing Hidden Failure Modes in Chest X-ray Classification via Spectral Domain Analysis
desc: Deep learning models for chest X-ray anomaly detection remain vulnerable to subtle distributional shifts (e.g., acquisition technique, patient-related factors, and preprocessing). Traditional error analysis often relies on semantic metadata or model embeddings, which can mask low-level signal variations that degrade performance. In this work, we propose a data-centric framework for automated failure mode discovery using spectral analysis. We project images into the frequency domain and extract a compact profile summarizing the distribution of signal energy across frequency bands. By performing unsupervised clustering on these spectral profiles, we demonstrate that model failures are not randomly distributed, but are strongly concentrated within specific spectral clusters. This method effectively isolates "blind spots", enabling the prediction of model reliability and the discovery of performance-degrading data slices without requiring ground-truth failure annotations.

title: Leveraging genomic deep learning models for the prediction of noncoding variant effects.
desc: [Nature genetics] Characterizing noncoding variant function remains an important challenge in human genetics. Genomic deep learning models have emerged as a promising approach to enable in silico prediction of variant effects. These models include supervised sequence-to-activity models, which predict molecular phenotypes such as genome-wide chromatin states or gene expression levels directly from DNA sequence, and self-supervised genomic language models. Here we review progress in leveraging these models for noncoding variant effect prediction. We describe practical considerations for making such predictions and categorize the types of ground-truth data used to evaluate variant effect predictions, providing insight into the settings in which current models are most useful. Our Review highlights key considerations for practitioners and opportunities for improvement in model development and evaluation.

title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
desc: Literature-searching language agents are becoming a standard component of scientific assistants for the life sciences, yet there is little controlled evidence on which parts of their harness matter. We run a controlled ablation on biomedical claim verification (SciFact) with the live PubMed API as the only tool. Holding the backbone and output format fixed, we compare four harnesses: closed-book answering, single-shot retrieval using the claim as the query, a ReAct-style agent that writes its own PubMed queries, and an oracle given the gold abstracts, each with two efficient frontier backbones. Naive single-shot retrieval finds the gold paper for only 6% of claims and turns overconfident errors into abstentions without improving accuracy. Letting the model formulate its own queries triples gold recall and yields the best verdicts (62% accuracy vs. 49-59% for the other realistic harnesses), although these differences are not significant at our sample size and agents use fewer than half of their search budget. With gold abstracts, the same models reach 79-86% accuracy, a significant 17-24 point gap showing that retrieval, not reasoning, is the main bottleneck. Finally, a citation audit shows that closed-book models cite PubMed IDs that almost always exist (327/335) but are almost never relevant: a cross-family LLM judge rates only 3 of 327 existing citations as relevant to the claim, versus 67% for citations produced by the search agent. Existence checks are therefore insufficient safeguards for scientific agents. We release code, prompts, and all cached tool calls at https://github.com/saqlain2204/real-pmids-wrong-papers.

title: A Large Language Model-Assisted Protocol for Metadata Classification and Governance in Electric Power Information Systems.
source: PubMed · Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
desc: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] Electric power organizations must classify heterogeneous data assets before applying access, retention, and cybersecurity controls. This study presents a metadata-only protocol that combines a fixed large language model (LLM) prompt, structured JSON output, deterministic screening, and mandatory human adjudication across five governance classes. The protocol was evaluated on 240 metadata records from 10 business domains. Raw LLM predictions agreed with adjudicated human labels for 207 records (86.25%; macro-F1 = 0.827), outperforming an exploratory deterministic rule baseline (66.67%) and a majority-class baseline (41.25%). Eighty-two records (34.17%) were routed to manual review; after adjudication, all 82 matched the reference labels. Five unsafe downgrades involved Critical Operational records and were intercepted by the review pathway. The workflow is limited to metadata and does not process raw documents, full tables, telemetry, or logs. These findings support LLM use as a triage aid rather than an autonomous classifier for metadata in electric power data governance.

title: How Ground Truth Shapes Retrieval Scores: Evidence-Aware Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Breast Lesions
desc: Purpose: To describe an evidence-aware retrieval evaluation protocol for a clinical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system over breast lesion management literature, addressing the dependence of retrieval scores on annotation coverage. Methods: An 18-document corpus and an 18-query development benchmark, with one Yes/No or WH-question per document, were used. Retrieval combined dense embeddings, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking. Chunk sizes of 128 to 1024 tokens, overlaps of 0 to 20%, and four retriever configurations were evaluated. Relevance was defined by evidence spans mapped to all containing chunks, treating overlapping chunks with equivalent evidence as relevant. Retrieval was evaluated using R-Precision, Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG@K. Separately, generation was assessed on a 512-token index at K=1 to 5 using DeepEval claim-level metrics, with deepseek-v4-pro as the LLM judge, and BLEU/ROUGE metrics. Results: The selected hybrid retriever, using 384-token chunks and 20% overlap, retrieved accepted evidence in the top three results for 17 of 18 queries. Recall@3, R-Precision, MRR@3, and nDCG@3 each reached 0.94. Ground-truth curation increased evidence spans from 25 to 37 and accepted chunk targets from 36 to 51 without changing retrieval rankings. Conclusion: Cross-encoder reranking achieved the highest retrieval scores. Expanded relevance annotations increased recognized evidence without changing rankings, highlighting annotation sensitivity. The small development set and retrieval-informed curation require independent validation, including radiologist assessment of evidence sufficiency.

title: Small variant calling in the era of long-read sequencing.
desc: [Nature reviews. Genetics] Long-read sequencing enables accurate analysis of complex and repetitive genomic regions but has distinct error profiles compared to short-read sequencing. Consequently, the tools for calling small variants - the predominant source of human genetic diversity - have shifted towards deep learning-based methods. This transition has reshaped variant calling across biological contexts, including germline, de novo, somatic and mosaic variants, and sequencing modalities for capturing both DNA and RNA at different resolutions. These deep learning frameworks are being developed in combination with alignment-based, assembly-based and pangenome-based strategies for small variant detection. In this Review, we chart the trajectory towards complete telomere-to-telomere profiling of small variants and consider the computational innovations needed to benchmark newly accessible repetitive regions and complex variants.

title: Evaluation of Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Software Ensembles for Hippocampal Segmentation
desc: Accurate hippocampal segmentation can be a useful tool for diagnosing and monitoring neurological conditions such as Alzheimer's disease and epilepsy. While numerous automated segmentation methods exist, their clinical adoption remains limited. Reliable uncertainty assessment can enhance trust and facilitate clinical translation. This study evaluates ensembles of five heterogeneous hippocampal segmentation methods - InnerEye, ASHS, FastSurfer, HippoSeg, and FreeSurfer - across two dementia datasets and one epilepsy dataset. The sub-ensemble containing InnerEye, FastSurfer, and HippoSeg emerged as both accurate and efficient, highlighting the feasibility of balancing computational cost and performance. Additionally, ensemble-derived uncertainty quantification with sample variance, mutual information, and predictive entropy is shown to reduce inaccurate segmentations by flagging low-confidence cases, potentially providing a mechanism for automatically escalating ambiguous cases for expert assessment. Lastly, this study explores the downstream clinical utility of ensemble-derived uncertainty, finding a significant correlation with motion artefact severity and a modest contribution to Alzheimer's disease classification.

title: Advanced cell-instructive bio-inks: Engineering multiscale niches for functional tissue formation.
desc: [Bioactive materials] Three-dimensional bioprinting has transformed tissue fabrication by enabling the precise spatial organization of living cells and biomaterials into biomimetic tissue constructs. However, advances in manufacturing have outpaced the development of bio-inks capable of actively directing tissue formation. Most existing bio-inks remain optimized for printability, rheological behaviour, and structural fidelity, while providing limited control over the biological processes that govern tissue morphogenesis, functional maturation, and regeneration. This review examines the emerging paradigm of cell-instructive bio-inks, which integrate biological regulation directly into material design to recreate the cellular microenvironments that guide tissue development. We present a unifying framework that classifies these bio-inks according to three complementary regulatory dimensions: biochemical niches that regulate cell fate through molecular signalling and regenerative matrices; architectural niches that direct tissue organization through spatial and structural cues; and metabolic niches that modulate oxygen availability, redox homeostasis, and cellular metabolism. We further discuss strategies for integrating these instructive functions within multifunctional bio-inks, together with scalable manufacturing, and artificial intelligence-assisted bio-ink design. By redefining bio-inks as active regulators of cellular behaviour, this review establishes a conceptual framework for engineering next-generation bio-inks capable of orchestrating tissue development, functional maturation, and regenerative outcomes.

title: Local Discrimination of Binary Classifiers via Localized AUC Functional
desc: Risk prediction models are frequently evaluated with AUC, which means that during evaluation we are blind to performance heterogeneity, which could lead to bad decision-making in clinics. In this work, we aim to change that by identifying patient cohorts for whom the risk prediction model might not be an accurate predictor. To separate these cohorts, we use a version of the weighted AUC, which we call Localized AUC or LAUC. Using this metric, we build a method that we coin LOCATOR. This method is able to identify cohorts of patients for whom the risk prediction model is inaccurate. We test this method both in real-world data and in simulations. We also build a statistical background for the use of Localized AUC for our purposes.

title: Insights into the structure-property relationships of biogel-based inks in 3D food printing: From hydrogels and oleogels to bigels.
source: PubMed · Advances in colloid and interface science
desc: [Advances in colloid and interface science] Three dimensional food printing (3DFP) enables the on-demand fabrication of edible constructs with customizable geometries, textures, and nutritional profiles. Biogel-based inks (BGink), including hydrogels, oleogels, and bigels, provide a highly versatile platform, as their rheological and physicochemical properties can be systematically tuned to meet specific processing and functional requirements. This review critically synthesizes recent advances in biogel-based 3DFP through a multiscale structure-property-function framework. It compares the roles of molecular crosslinking and water confinement in hydrogels, oil-structuring networks in oleogels, and phase organization and interfacial coupling in bigels, linking these structural mechanisms to ink properties and macroscopic functionality. Building upon these colloidal and interfacial architectures, the discussion then connects formulation-dependent properties with key printing parameters to explain the shape fidelity, structural stability, and sensory-related and functional properties of printed structures. These structure-function relationships are further discussed in the context of representative applications, including personalized and functional foods, clinical and therapeutic diets, artificial intelligence integration, and sustainable biomanufacturing. Current limitations and future research needs are also identified. Overall, this review clarifies the multiscale relationships among biogel microstructures, ink properties, and end-product performance, providing a scientific foundation for the rational design of next-generation BGink and advanced 3DFP systems.

title: A General-Purpose Dual-Path Interaction Framework for Multi-View Medical Image Segmentation: Alleviating Data Volume Dependency in Small-Sample Regimes
desc: The performance of medical image segmentation depends on a large amount of annotated data, and most segmentation models experience a significant drop in performance in low-sample-size scenarios. Existing semi-supervised and weakly supervised methods rely on specific network architectures, while traditional multi-view-assisted segmentation methods require strictly paired samples, which limits their clinical applications. To address these issues, we propose DPIF, a general-purpose plug-and-play dual-path interaction framework compatible with arbitrary encoder-decoder segmentation networks, which leverages cross-view anatomical complementarity to reduce annotation reliance. DPIF first performs Sinkhorn optimal transport-based cross-view distribution alignment to establish global semantic correspondence without sample-level pairing. It then adopts conditional mutual information-guided feature decoupling to enable bidirectional knowledge transfer only within the shared semantic space, suppressing view-specific noise. Finally, persistent homology-based topological regularization encodes anatomical invariants as unsupervised priors to mitigate overfitting. Experiments were conducted using 24 baseline models on a private multicenter echocardiography dataset and two public datasets. The results show that DPIF-enhanced models outperform single-view baseline models when trained on comparable amounts of data. Notably, most dual-path variants trained on 40\% - 60\% of the data achieve performance comparable to that of single-view models trained on the full dataset. This demonstrates that DPIF provides a general-purpose and scalable solution for data-scarce multi-view medical image segmentation problems.

title: Fast and accurate taxonomic domain assignment of short metagenomic reads using BBERT.
desc: [Nucleic acids research] Shotgun metagenomes from complex environments such as soil uncover vast biodiversity. Yet most short reads produced by shotgun sequencing cannot be taxonomically or functionally annotated, as they lack a sufficiently comprehensive reference, obscuring the true structure and function of microbial communities. We introduce BBERT, a nucleotide large language model optimized for short reads. Testing on a large cohort of soil metagenomes, we found that BBERT identifies bacterial sequence syntax without relying on reference databases, enabling accurate assignment of taxonomic domain, coding potential, and reading frame directly from reads as short as 100 bp. BBERT is small and fast enough to analyze metagenomes using a modest GPU and can be used to convert short metagenomic reads directly to bacterial amino acid sequences for downstream applications. BBERT also improves de novo metagenomic assembly, reducing mismatches and gaps while accelerating runtime. Using metagenomes from wild legume nodules, we demonstrate that BBERT filtering improves bin quality while significantly accelerating de novo assembly. By providing fast, reference-free classification of short reads, BBERT unlocks large metagenomic archives for more accurate ecological and evolutionary analyses.

title: When Annotation Patterns Are Learned: Skin-Tone Dependence in Dermatology Concepts
desc: Concept bottleneck models (CBMs) let clinicians inspect and correct skin disease diagnoses through clinical concepts, but only if the concept annotations are reliable. We therefore audit the reliability of SkinCon, a widely used dermatology concept dataset, across skin tones. Within the same disease and with near duplicates removed, erythema is annotated far less often on dark than on light skin, with an odds ratio of 0.17. In contrast, hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation are annotated more often, with odds ratios of 6.2 and 4.5, respectively. We refer to this pattern as tone-dependent concept annotation. An evidential concept model trained on these annotations learns the same pattern and reproduces it on unseen images. Such a model may agree with potential erythema omissions rather than contradict them. Consistent with this, three label error detectors underperform a disease-only baseline at finding erythema that dermatologist captions mention but SkinCon labels as absent. The three detectors are based on confident learning, training dynamics, and the model's own evidential uncertainty. Concept annotations should thus be audited within each subgroup before explanations built on them can be trusted.

title: Fundus camera and artificial intelligence for diabetic retinopathy screening in a São Paulo shelter.
source: PubMed · Revista da Associacao Medica Brasileira (1992)
desc: [Revista da Associacao Medica Brasileira (1992)] The aim of this study was to evaluate the applicability of a smartphone-based portable fundus camera for diabetic retinopathy screening in elderly residents of a specialized shelter in São Paulo, Brazil, considering image acquisition by non-ophthalmologist professionals and remote case classification. Prospective pilot interventional study at the Centro de Acolhida Especial para Idosos Morada São João. Thirty-eight participants (76 eyes) underwent retinal imaging using the Eyer® portable fundus camera (Phelcom Technologies, Brazil) by trained non-ophthalmologist professionals. Images were remotely evaluated by a retinal specialist and compared to the EyerMaps® artificial intelligence system. Mean age was 71.6±7.0 years; 78.9% male. Fifteen participants (39.5%) had confirmed diabetes mellitus. The specialist identified abnormalities in 70 of 76 eyes (92.1%), most frequently glaucoma suspicion, media opacity suggestive of cataract, chorioretinal changes, and age-related macular degeneration signs; no diabetic retinopathy was identified. Against the specialist's assessment of any ocular abnormality as the reference standard, the artificial intelligence system classified 22 eyes as abnormal, yielding sensitivity 25.7% (95%CI 16.9-37.0), specificity 33.3% (95%CI 9.7-70.0), positive predictive value 81.8% (95%CI 61.5-92.7), negative predictive value 3.7% (95%CI 1.0-12.5), and overall accuracy 26.3% (95%CI 17.7-37.2). The Eyer® device demonstrated operational feasibility for ocular screening by trained non-ophthalmologists. The high prevalence of media opacities and non-diabetic retinopathy conditions compromised artificial intelligence performance, highlighting the need for broader screening strategies in elderly and socially vulnerable populations.

title: CVP-BAA: Efficiently Adapting Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation
desc: Various task-specific medical segmentation models have demonstrated strong performance, their heavy reliance on extensive annotations and highly specialized architectures limits their versatility, scalability, and clinical applicability. Recently, adapting vision foundation models, particularly the segment anything model (SAM), has emerged as a promising alternative. However, prevalent parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, such as prompt tuning and adapter tuning, often lack an explicit mechanism to embed local structural priors into the long-range dependency modeling of vision transformers (ViT), rendering them insufficiently sensitive to fine-grained details. To address these limitations, we introduce CVP-BAA, a novel hybrid PEFT method that improves SAM's sensitivity to domain-specific textures and local details, leading to superior boundary delineation. The proposed CVP-BAA adopts two key ideas. First, it introduces a convolutional visual prompting (CVP) strategy that leverages convolutional features as structural priors, prepending them to the key and value projections within the multi-head self-attention layers of strategically selected ViT blocks. Through a dedicated prompt generation-and-injection module, this mechanism effectively bridges local spatial details with global context semantics. Second, a boundary-aware adapter (BAA) is designed as a parallel branch to the feed-forward network within the same selected blocks. By explicitly computing and amplifying high-frequency components, the BAA enhances feature representations along tissue boundaries and fine-grained lesion structures. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks across three imaging modalities demonstrate that CVP-BAA achieves superior segmentation performance, surpassing existing task-specific models and PEFT-based SAM adaptations in both quantitative metrics and qualitative results.

title: Global forest typology at 10-meter resolution for forest and land-use monitoring.
desc: [Scientific data] Distinguishing forest types-primary, naturally regenerating, planted, and plantation forests-from agricultural tree crops and other land uses is essential for carbon accounting, biodiversity assessment, conservation planning, and supply-chain regulation. However, no existing global dataset resolves this typology at high spatial resolution. We present the Forest Typology (ForTy) v1 dataset, a global 10-meter resolution baseline map for 2020 that classifies all land into six categories aligned with FAO and EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) definitions: Primary Forest, Naturally Regenerating Forest, Planted Forest, Plantation Forest, Tree Crops and Agroforestry, and Other Land. A cascaded deep learning pipeline, trained on 1.7 million globally distributed samples, generates per-class relative confidence maps from geospatial satellite embeddings by combining weakly supervised learning with active learning. Independent validation against 8,190 expert-labeled stratified random sites yields an overall accuracy of 90.2% for the six-class scheme, 94.8% for natural forest classification, and 95.5% for forest/non-forest classification.

title: Equivariant Experience Replay for Continual Learning in Imaging Inverse Problems
desc: In this work, we propose Equivariant Experience Replay, a new paradigm for achieving continual learning of deep networks for solving ill-posed imaging inverse problems. Inspired by recent advances on unsupervised learning methods such as equivariant imaging/splitting, we find the exploitation of group-symmetry structure is particularly relevant and effective in continual learning setting for ill-posed inversion tasks. We therefore propose this new experience replay scheme, which is tailored for such inverse problems. Our numerical study demonstrates the superiority of our method compared to existing continual learning methods for inverse problems in medical imaging and image processing.

title: The Differential That Never Gets Generated.
desc: [International journal of dermatology] Residents increasingly ask large language models to name a lesion before diagnosing it themselves. The practice contributes a specific harm: never-skilling, a phenomenon in which reasoning is never acquired, and is distinct from 'deskilling' or 'model error'. Forming a differential first is necessary but insufficient. Departments should require documented differentials, supervise disagreement, and examine unassisted reasoning.

title: Text-Only LLM Correctors Break Correct Transcripts: A Repair-Damage Analysis of Audio Grounding in ASR Error Correction
desc: LLM correctors of ASR output are judged by aggregate WER, which hides what they fix and what they break. We decompose every WER change exactly into repaired tokens, damaged tokens and insertions, and use this to ask what the source audio adds to a corrector. We compare correction with and without the audio, for the model's own draft and for the output of an independent recogniser, on three corpora. With Gemini 2.5 Flash, text-only correction of its own draft breaks 13-32% of already-correct transcripts; with the audio, 1-3%. Damage falls in both settings. Repair falls against the own draft and rises against the recogniser. On medical dictation, kept insertions cancel the gain in net WER. The open-weight Voxtral, which rarely edits, does not show this pattern. Prompts differ between the two arms, so the contrasts bound the effect of the audio and do not isolate it.

title: Plausible but Unimplantable: A Trustworthiness Audit of Shape Completion Foundation Models for Cranial Defect Reconstruction
desc: A patient who has lost part of the skull vault needs an implant that fits the defect exactly, and such implants are still drawn by hand in CAD by specialists, which makes each case slow and expensive. The task can be considered as a shape completion problem, so pretrained completion models, and now the first shape completion foundation models, look like a way to remove that manual step. We audited three publicly released pretrained shape completion models, two of them foundation models, applied zero-shot to 239 cranial defects, some carved from public skull datasets and some real post-craniectomy cases. Each output was compared with simply returning the patient's own remaining bone, and tested for whether the predicted material could be placed without intersecting the bone that is still there. On the 210 carved defects none of the three improved on doing nothing, and on the 29 real cases only one did so beyond chance. Yet not one output, from any model in any configuration, was implantable: none managed both to stay clear of the bone the patient still has and to place more material than doing nothing, where a task-specific volumetric model, trained for this task and selected on these cases, was implantable on all but one. The output that most convincingly resembles a skull is no more placeable than the rest, and at these point densities implant thickness cannot be read off the emitted points at all, which is a property of the output representation rather than of any one model. On this evidence the shape completion foundation models we could obtain cannot be trusted and, used as released, are not usable in clinical practice. Substantial research towards trustworthy foundation models for shape completion is still needed.

title: When Reconstruction Is Not Enough: Doubly Robust Counterfactual and Interventional Mediation Analysis with Learned Multimodal Representations
desc: Learned representations of high-dimensional multimodal health records are increasingly used to adjust for confounding, yet they are usually trained to reconstruct the data rather than preserve the information that causal identification requires. We study counterfactual outcomes under alternative treatments, including phenotype-specific effects and patient-level counterfactual risk profiles of the kind digital twins provide, and interventional direct and indirect effects under exposure-induced intermediate confounding. We give conditions under which a representation preserves identification and show that interventional mediation is more demanding than counterfactual comparison. We prove that no covariate-only training objective, whether reconstruction, contrastive, or physics-informed, can certify that a representation is sufficient, and that, in a linear structural model, a representation can lose arbitrarily little reconstruction accuracy yet induce arbitrarily large bias. We decompose the error of cross-fitted doubly robust estimators into a first-order representation bias, which neither double robustness nor cross-fitting removes, and a second-order remainder of nuisance-estimation errors, so coverage worsens as the sample size grows when the representation is insufficient. We propose a workflow combining modality-specific variational autoencoders trained outside the estimation sample, cross-fitted doubly robust estimators, locked phenotypes, select-then-confirm pathway analysis, portable representations, and diagnostics for representation insufficiency, exposure leakage, and sensitivity. In simulations, discarding a rare, moderately strong confounder gave indirect-effect intervals with 2% coverage at n = 3,000; reconstruction loss missed the problem, and a simple predictive diagnostic flagged it in every replicate.

title: Learning to Reason Like a Cytopathologist:Clinically Grounded Multiscale Evidential Learning for Cervical Cytology
desc: Cervical cytology presents a fundamentally ambiguous diagnostic landscape, where equivocal categories such as Atypical Squamous Cells of Undetermined Significance (ASC-US) occupy a morphological grey zone that is definitional. For clinical decision support, the goal extends beyond assigning a definitive label to every sample: cases must also be distinguished by whether the available evidence supports a confident decision or warrants further consideration, a distinction conventional classification models are not designed to explicitly represent. We propose a multiscale evidential framework that models cervical cytology along an ordinal disease continuum using clinically grounded soft anchors, representing progression from benign reactive changes to precancerous lesions and malignancy. Three biologically motivated spatial contexts--nuclear morphology, cytoplasmic characteristics, and neighbourhood cellular architecture--are independently encoded using a shared frozen DINOv2 backbone, preserving inter-scale disagreement that early fusion may obscure. Calibrated predictions are transformed into Dempster--Shafer belief masses and fused with reliability discounting, allowing conflicting evidence and insufficient support to remain explicitly uncommitted rather than forcing a decision. The fused belief state drives interpretable routing that separates confidently classified cases from those with irreducible evidential insufficiency, enabling clinically meaningful triage. Across two independent publicly available conventional cytology datasets, RIVA and CRIC Cervix, the framework generalises consistently, with uncertainty strongly associated with diagnostic difficulty: incorrect predictions carry 1.94x-4.13x higher uncertainty than correct ones.

title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
desc: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. Existing approaches often trade off verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability. We introduce $\textbf{SpectralCanary}$, which uses a smooth low-pass mask to blend a fixed canary image into every collection image while leaving captions unchanged and requiring neither auxiliary generation nor per-image optimization. A lightweight verifier detects the transferred signal in suspect-model outputs. Across eight tests on the Pokemon dataset and three realistic data transformations, spanning two architectures families, SpectralCanary achieves the highest average per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR ($91.1\%$) and fixed threshold model-level accuracy using 30 generations ($94.8\%$) among the evaluated methods. Across five datasets spanning artistic, medical, satellite, and fashion domains with SD3.5, SpectralCanary averages $92.4\%$ per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR while preserving the released images (SSIM $0.989$, LPIPS $0.022$) with a near-zero mean change FID (mean $Δ$FID $0.05$) across datasets. Matched-energy ablations on Pokemon and ROCOv2 support our design choice, low-frequency placement transfers more reliably compared to mid/high-frequency placement. Under the evaluated adaptive attacks, the most effective removal requires aggressive modification and incurs more than $25$ $Δ$FID points. These results identify low-frequency visual signals as effective carriers for collection-level T2I audit traces.

title: From Prompt Rules to Golden Data Model: Production-Scale Generation of Personalized, Compliant Pharmaceutical Claims
desc: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate domain-specific commercial & medical content (e.g., claims, statements, and promotional phrases) in regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals. However, ensuring its regulatory compliance, factual accuracy, and audience-specific personalization remains a major challenge. We report a production case study asking whether moving compliance and personalization signal from prompt-level rules into retrieval time structured context improves pharmaceutical claims generation, using Composer, a deployed internal tool built on a Golden Data Model (GDM) of 1,867 pharmaceutical claims spanning four products. The GDM integrates claim metadata, references, audience labels, material type, usage history, Match Text Variant (MTV) links, and a six dimension quality score (6C). Across six product-audience segments, the context pipeline improves intended indication (+29%), intended content type (+62%) and intended target audience (+67%), 6C quality score (+86%), and claim reuse (+34%). Production log analysis over the deployment period shows a 29.5% reduction in weekly API cost. We report this as descriptive deployment evidence. This work is a systems and data architecture contribution: it shows that in a regulated, high-stakes domain, restructuring claim data for retrieval-time filtering is a more scalable lever than expanding prompt-level rules, and documents the engineering path data cleaning, graph linking, and quality scoring.

title: Speculative Acceptance Does Not Decay with Position: A Full-Length Diagnostic on Long Chain-of-Thought with Independent Drafts
desc: The claim that speculative-decoding acceptance rate decays as a chain-of-thought grows longer has become a de facto industry narrative, motivating draft-model co-design and position-aware training. Nearly all direct evidence comes from trained drafters whose offline training length is far shorter than inference, so a purely positional law has never been isolated. We present the first systematic, full-length measurement of acceptance rate as a function of generation position on MATH-500 (all 500 problems), under greedy and sampling decoding, with two independent drafts against DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B: a same-family draft (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) and a cross-family draft (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct), yielding about 1.78M verification rounds. Using within-problem paired tests, we find that after isolating a greedy-decoding repetition pathology, acceptance rate does not decay with position in any of the four configurations within the supported ranges (greedy 0-8K, sampling 0-12K); the second half of each trajectory is slightly but significantly higher than the first. A controlled temperature sweep shows that the apparent sampling-mode degradation of high-entropy reflection tokens is a visibility artifact of argmax agreement, not a drop in expected acceptance probability. Rejections concentrate with high precision on reflection trigger tokens such as "wait", "however" and "check", an entropy-selective failure that a lightweight three-arm LoRA trajectory-alignment intervention (uniform, reflection-marked, entropy-weighted) fails to improve in mean accepted length. We thus supply the positional baseline that independent draft-target pairs were missing, and localize the residual failure to decision-point entropy rather than position.

title: AcoustiPrint: Physics-Guided Neural Design of Manufacturable Acoustic Structures
desc: Recent work in additive manufacturing and neural inverse design enables the creation of complex three-dimensional structures to manipulate physical fields, yet these designs must also adhere to discrete, non-differentiable fabrication constraints. Current methods limit the design space by imposing differentiable soft manufacturability loss penalties, or by fixing structures through post-processing, causing a discrepancy between the geometry optimized by the physics model and the final fabricated result. Thus, we present AcoustiPrint, a physics-informed neural architecture for constrained inverse design that represents three-dimensional geometries with an implicit neural representation (INR) and passes each candidate through a printability operator before evaluating its final response. The printability operator executes layer-wise self-support, discrete material selection, and whole-body connectivity, assuring fabrication feasibility. To allow for backpropagation through the discrete non-differentiable operations, we use surrogate gradients for the backward pass and a self-supervised printability objective that progressively drives the INR toward a valid design domain. We demonstrate AcoustiPrint for personalized transcranial focused ultrasound, where inter-patient differences in acoustic properties and head geometry deform wave propagation and requires patient-specific acoustic focusing. AcoustiPrint jointly optimizes three-dimensional geometry and material composition through differentiable wave physics while ensuring manufacturability. Experiments show manufacturable acoustic structures with enhanced focal accuracy and over density-based and phase-based baselines, demonstrating a generalized methodology for neural design through non-differentiable manufacturing constraints and differentiable physics.

title: Learning to Measure and Diagnose: A Clinical-Dictionary Radiomic Bottleneck Model for Thyroid Nodule Classification
desc: Thyroid ultrasound supports the assessment of nodule malignancy, but classification predictions often lack evidence linked to familiar clinical descriptions. Radiomics provides explicitly defined measurements that can support such explanations through a clinical dictionary. However, using these measurements as interpretable evidence requires reliable estimation from ultrasound images and preservation of measurement fidelity when optimizing classification performance. We propose a clinical-dictionary radiomic bottleneck model for thyroid nodule classification. Within this model, Family-Aware Radiomic Learning (FARL) estimates measurements with balanced supervision across feature families. Fidelity-Guided Bottleneck Modeling (FGBM) constructs a fixed bottleneck, followed by joint optimization of measurement estimation and classification under fidelity guidance. Decision evidence decomposition then traces feature contributions through a linear classifier and organizes them by clinical dictionary categories. Experiments on ThyroidXL and TN3K show competitive classification performance, while case studies illustrate feature contributions for benign and malignant nodules. These findings indicate interpretable classification with inspectable quantitative evidence informed by clinical knowledge. Code is available online.

title: Reliability-Aware Probabilistic Fusion for Multimodal Learning with Incomplete Evidence
desc: Multimodal inputs may be missing or degraded, raising distinct questions of evidence availability and trust. We introduce a reliability-aware Gaussian Product-of-Experts (PoE) in which an input-dependent reliability weight tempers each modality's latent precision, while missing experts are omitted. We characterize how reliability and availability affect posterior information and expert influence. Across two clinical multimodal tasks, the full framework remains competitive with complete inputs and achieves its clearest mean-AUROC advantage under modality absence, particularly on HAIM-MIMIC-MM. Ablations show a substantial gain from missing-aware training and an additional HAIM improvement from reliability weighting under matched PoE, missing-aware, and consistency training. Unseen test-time corruptions are used diagnostically and reveal modality-dependent reliability-weight and latent-uncertainty responses, including failure under severe degradation. Thus, reliability weighting provides an explicit evidence-control mechanism, while learning dependable quality signals remains an open challenge.

title: TernScope: Model-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient Ternary Endoscopic Segmentation
desc: Edge medical segmentation must reconcile small model size, high accuracy, and fast inference. TernScope addresses this tradeoff through model--hardware co-design, learning a compact segmentation network whose low-bit operators also simplify hardware execution. Split-channel large-kernel blocks preserve spatial context with limited computation, while branch fusion removes redundant inference paths. Ternary Progressive Quantization-aware Training (TPQ) then adapts the fused network from deep to shallow layers, through the decoder, and finally to the input and prediction layers. All 25 convolutions use ternary weights and 8-bit activations, enabling packed storage and multiplier-free computation. The resulting model uses 0.2483 M parameters and 0.0949 GMACs while retaining competitive segmentation accuracy on in-domain and external datasets. Under the same 45 nm technology, TernScope reduces compute-array area by 88.46% compared with the original Gemmini, a systolic-array accelerator with 8-bit $\times$ 8-bit multipliers. These results demonstrate a path from accurate lightweight medical segmentation to compact low-bit hardware.
